sentences.zh: 顧憲成，字叔時，無錫人。

translations.literal: Gu Xiancheng, styled Shushi, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiancheng, whose style was Shushi, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wanli he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Wanli reign he ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 八年成進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正病，朝士群為之禱，憲成不可。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng fell ill, court officials thronged to pray for him; Xiancheng would not.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng fell ill, officials throughout the court flocked to pray for his recovery; Xiancheng refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 同官代之署名，憲成手削去之。

translations.literal: A colleague signed his name in his place; Xiancheng personally struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: A colleague signed his name on his behalf; Xiancheng personally struck the name out.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，改吏部主事。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel as a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was transferred to a secretary's post in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 請告歸三年，補驗封主事。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned home for three years, then was reassigned as secretary in the Sealing and Investiture section.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and returned home for three years, then was reassigned as secretary in the Sealing and Investiture section.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大計京朝官，都御史辛自修掌計事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the great triennial evaluation of capital officials was held; Censor-in-Chief Xin Zixiu presided over the review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the great triennial evaluation of capital officials was held, with Censor-in-Chief Xin Zixiu in charge of the proceedings.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書何起鳴在拾遺中，自修坐是失執政意。

translations.literal: Minister of Works He Qiming was among those listed for recall in the supplementary review; because of this Zixiu lost favor with the chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works He Qiming was named in the supplementary recall list, and for this Zixiu lost the favor of the chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳與郊承風旨並論起鳴、自修，實以攻自修而庇起鳴。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Yuhe, following their intent, impeached both Qiming and Zixiu—actually to attack Zixiu while shielding Qiming.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Yuhe, following their intent, impeached both Qiming and Zixiu—in reality to strike at Zixiu while protecting Qiming.

sentences.zh: 於是二人並罷，並責御史糾起鳴者四人。

translations.literal: Thereupon both men were dismissed together, and four censors who had impeached Qiming were also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon both men were dismissed, and four censors who had impeached Qiming were punished as well.

sentences.zh: 憲成不平，上疏語侵執政，被旨切責，謫桂陽州判官。

translations.literal: Xiancheng was indignant and submitted a memorial with language offensive to the chief administrators; by imperial order he was sternly rebuked and demoted to assistant magistrate of Guiyang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, Xiancheng submitted a memorial whose language offended the chief administrators; by imperial order he was sternly rebuked and demoted to assistant magistrate of Guiyang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 稍遷處州推官。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to supervising secretary of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to supervising secretary of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，補泉州推官。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning; when the mourning period ended he was reassigned as supervising secretary of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he observed mourning; after the mourning period he was reassigned as supervising secretary of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉公廉第一。

translations.literal: He was rated first for public integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was rated first for public integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢吏部考功主事，歷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretary in the Personnel Ministry's Merit Evaluation section, and rose through the ranks to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Personnel's Merit Evaluation section and rose through the ranks to vice director.

sentences.zh: 會有詔三皇子並封王。

translations.literal: At this time there came an edict ennobling all three imperial sons as kings simultaneously.
translations.idiomatic: At this time an edict came down to ennoble all three imperial sons as princes at once.

sentences.zh: 憲成偕同官上疏曰：

translations.literal: Xiancheng together with his colleagues submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng and his colleagues submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 皇上因《祖訓》立嫡之條，欲暫令三皇子並封王，以待有嫡立嫡，無嫡立長。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, relying on the ancestral instruction's provision for establishing the heir by the legitimate wife, wishes temporarily to ennoble all three princes as kings, to wait until there is a legitimate son born to the empress—then establish the legitimate son as heir, and if there is no legitimate son establish the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, invoking the ancestral instruction's rule on establishing the heir by the legitimate line, wishes temporarily to ennoble all three princes at once, to wait until a son of the empress is born—then establish the legitimate son as heir, and if there is none, establish the eldest.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏而思之，「待」之一言，有大不可者。

translations.literal: We your ministers bow and consider: the word "wait" alone contains much that absolutely cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers bow low and reflect: in the single word "wait" there is much that must not be done.

sentences.zh: 太子，天下本。

translations.literal: The heir apparent is the foundation of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent is the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 豫定太子，所以固本。

translations.literal: To establish the heir in advance is how the foundation is secured.
translations.idiomatic: To establish the heir in advance is how that foundation is secured.

sentences.zh: 是故有嫡立嫡，無嫡立長，就見在論是也，待將來則非也。

translations.literal: Therefore "if there is a legitimate son establish the legitimate son, if not establish the eldest" applies when judging the situation as it now stands; to wait for the future is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Thus "if there is a legitimate son, establish the legitimate son; if not, establish the eldest" applies when judging the present situation; to wait for the future is not correct.

sentences.zh: 我朝建儲家法，東宮不待嫡，元子不並封。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's established practice for creating an heir: the Eastern Palace does not wait for a son of the legitimate line; the eldest son is not ennobled together with others.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's established practice for creating an heir holds that the Eastern Palace does not wait for a son of the legitimate line, and the eldest son is not ennobled together with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 廷臣言甚詳，皇上概弗省，豈皇上創見有加列聖之上乎？

translations.literal: Court ministers spoke at great length; Your Majesty wholly paid no heed—does Your Majesty have a novel view surpassing all the sage emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers have spoken at length, yet Your Majesty has paid no heed to any of it. Does Your Majesty intend a novel departure rising above all the sage emperors of old?

sentences.zh: 有天下者稱天子，天子之元子稱太子。

translations.literal: He who possesses the realm is called Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven's eldest son is called heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He who possesses the realm is called Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven's eldest son is called heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 天子系乎天，君與天一體也；

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is bound to Heaven—the ruler and Heaven are one body;
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven is bound to Heaven—the ruler and Heaven are one body;

sentences.zh: 太子系乎父，父子一體也。

translations.literal: the heir apparent is bound to the father—father and son are one body.
translations.idiomatic: the heir apparent is bound to the father—father and son are one body.

sentences.zh: 主鬯承祧，於是乎在，不可得而爵。

translations.literal: The one who presides over the ancestral sacrifices and continues the line lies here; he cannot be given a mere noble title.
translations.idiomatic: He who presides over the ancestral sacrifices and continues the line is defined here; he cannot be reduced to a mere noble title.

sentences.zh: 今欲並封三王，元子之封何所系乎？

translations.literal: Now if you wish to ennoble all three princes together, to what is the eldest son's ennoblement attached?
translations.idiomatic: If you now wish to ennoble all three princes at once, to what is the eldest son's ennoblement attached?

sentences.zh: 無所系，則難乎其為名；

translations.literal: If attached to nothing, then it is hard to make a name for it;
translations.idiomatic: If attached to nothing, it is hard to make the title mean anything;

sentences.zh: 有所系，則難乎其為實。

translations.literal: if attached to something, then it is hard to make the reality of it.
translations.idiomatic: if attached to something, it is hard to make the reality match.

sentences.zh: 皇上以為權宜雲耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes this to be but an expedient measure.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes this to be merely an expedient.

sentences.zh: 夫權宜者，不得已而行之也。

translations.literal: An expedient is what one does only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: An expedient is what one does only when there is no alternative.

sentences.zh: 元子為太子，諸子為藩王，於理順，於分稱，於情安，有何不得已而然乎？

translations.literal: The eldest son as heir, the other sons as feudal princes—in reason it is orderly, in status fitting, in affection secure—what necessity forces such a course?
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son as heir, the other sons as feudal princes—in reason it is orderly, in rank fitting, in affection secure—what necessity forces any other course?

sentences.zh: 耦尊鈞大，逼所由生。

translations.literal: Two equal in honor press greatly upon the one from whom they sprang.
translations.idiomatic: Two equals in honor weigh heavily upon the one who bore them.

sentences.zh: 皇上以《祖訓》為法，子孫以皇上為法。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes the ancestral instructions as law; posterity will take Your Majesty as law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes the ancestral instructions as law; posterity will take Your Majesty as law.

sentences.zh: 皇上不難創其所無，後世詎難襲其所有？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not shrink from creating what never existed, will posterity shrink from copying whatever exists?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not shrink from creating what never existed, will posterity shrink from copying whatever you establish?

sentences.zh: 自是而往，幸皆有嫡可也，不然，是無東宮也。

translations.literal: From this point onward, if fortunately there is always a legitimate son it may be well; otherwise, there will be no Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: From this point onward, if fortunately there is always a legitimate son, all may be well; otherwise there will be no Eastern Palace at all.

sentences.zh: 又幸而如皇上之英明可也，不然，凡皇子皆東宮也，無乃啟萬世之大患乎？

translations.literal: And if fortunately there is a sovereign as enlightened as Your Majesty it may be well; otherwise, every prince will be the Eastern Palace—will this not open a great calamity for ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: And if fortunately there is a sovereign as enlightened as Your Majesty, all may be well; otherwise every prince will be the Eastern Palace—will this not open a great calamity for ten thousand generations?

sentences.zh: 皇后與皇上共承宗祧，期於宗祧得人而已。

translations.literal: The empress and Your Majesty jointly sustain the ancestral sacrifices, expecting only that the line receive the right man.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and Your Majesty jointly sustain the ancestral line, expecting only that the line receive the right man.

sentences.zh: 皇上之元子諸子，即皇后之元子諸子。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's eldest son and other sons are likewise the empress's eldest and other sons.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's eldest son and other sons are likewise the empress's eldest and other sons.

sentences.zh: 恭妃、皇貴妃不得而私之，統於尊也。

translations.literal: Lady Gong and the honored consort cannot privately claim them—they are unified under the one who is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gong and the honored consort cannot claim them as their private sons; they are unified under the one who is honored.

sentences.zh: 豈必如輔臣王錫爵之請，須拜皇后為母，而後稱子哉？

translations.literal: Must it be as Grand Secretary Wang Xijue requested, that they must first acknowledge the empress as mother and only then be called sons?
translations.idiomatic: Must it be as Grand Secretary Wang Xijue requested—that they must first acknowledge the empress as mother before they may be called sons?

sentences.zh: 況始者奉旨，少待二三年而已，俄改二十年，又改於二十一年，然猶可以歲月期也。

translations.literal: Moreover, at first an edict said to wait but two or three years; soon it was changed to twenty years, then changed again to twenty-one years—yet one could still mark it by the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at first the edict said to wait only two or three years; soon it was changed to twenty, then to twenty-one—yet one could still reckon it by the calendar.

sentences.zh: 今曰「待嫡」，是未可以歲月期也。

translations.literal: Now to say "wait for the legitimate heir" is something that cannot be marked by the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Now to say "wait for the legitimate heir" is something that cannot be reckoned by the calendar at all.

sentences.zh: 命方布而忽更，意屢遷而愈緩。

translations.literal: Orders are just promulgated and suddenly altered; intentions shift repeatedly and grow ever lax.
translations.idiomatic: Orders are barely promulgated before they are changed; intentions shift again and again and grow ever more lax.

sentences.zh: 自並封命下，叩閽上封事者不可勝數，至裏巷小民亦聚族而竊議，是孰使之然哉？

translations.literal: Since the simultaneous-enfeoffment order was issued, those who beat the palace gates and submitted sealed memorials are beyond count—even common folk in the lanes gather by clan to whisper about it. Who made this happen?
translations.idiomatic: Since the order for simultaneous enfeoffment was issued, those who beat the palace gates and submitted sealed memorials are beyond counting—even common folk in the lanes gather by clan to whisper about it. Who made this happen?

sentences.zh: 人心之公也。

translations.literal: It is the fairness of people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: It is the fairness of people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 而皇上猶責輔臣以擔當。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty still reproaches the grand secretaries for lacking backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty still reproaches the grand secretaries for lacking backbone.

sentences.zh: 錫爵夙夜趣召，乃排群議而順上旨，豈所謂擔當？

translations.literal: Xijue, hurrying day and night at the summons, instead excluded the multitude of opinions to follow the imperial intent—is this what is called backbone?
translations.idiomatic: Xijue, hurrying day and night at the summons, excluded the multitude of opinions to follow the imperial intent—is this what is called backbone?

sentences.zh: 必積誠感悟納皇上於無過之地，乃真擔當耳。

translations.literal: Only by accumulating sincerity to move and draw Your Majesty into a place without fault is true backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Only by accumulating sincerity to move Your Majesty and draw him into a place without fault is true backbone.

sentences.zh: 不然，皇上且不能如天下何，而況錫爵哉！

translations.literal: Otherwise, Your Majesty will not be able to answer to the realm—how much less Xijue!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Your Majesty will not be able to answer to the realm—how much less Xijue!

sentences.zh: 皇上神明天縱，非溺寵狎昵之比。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's divine clarity was Heaven-given; he is not of the sort who dotes excessively or treats intimates lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's divine clarity was Heaven-given; you are not one who dotes excessively or treats intimates lightly.

sentences.zh: 而不諒者，見影而疑形，聞響而疑聲，即臣等亦有不能為皇上解者。

translations.literal: Yet those who do not understand see a shadow and suspect a form, hear a sound and suspect its source—even we your ministers have points we cannot explain on Your Majesty's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who do not understand see a shadow and suspect a form, hear a sound and suspect its source—even we your ministers have points we cannot explain on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 皇上盛德大業，比隆三五。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's great virtue and great enterprise rival the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's great virtue and great enterprise rival the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 而乃來此意外之紛紛，不亦惜乎！

translations.literal: Yet to come to this unexpected uproar—is it not a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Yet to come to this unexpected uproar—is it not a pity!

sentences.zh: 伏乞令皇元子早正儲位，皇第三子、皇第五子各就王爵。

translations.literal: We humbly beg that the imperial eldest son be established early in the heir's position, and that the third and fifth imperial sons each receive their princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg that the imperial eldest son be established early as heir, and that the third and fifth imperial sons each receive their princely titles.

sentences.zh: 父父子子，君君臣臣，兄兄弟弟。

translations.literal: Father as father, son as son; ruler as ruler, subject as subject; elder brother as elder brother, younger brother as younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Father as father, son as son; ruler as ruler, subject as subject; elder brother as elder brother, younger brother as younger brother.

sentences.zh: 宗廟之福，社稷之慶，悉在是矣。

translations.literal: The blessing of the ancestral temple and the rejoicing of the altars of soil and grain—all lie in this.
translations.idiomatic: The blessing of the ancestral temple and the rejoicing of the altars of soil and grain—all lie in this.

sentences.zh: 憲成又遺書錫爵，反覆辨論。

translations.literal: Xiancheng also sent a letter to Xijue, arguing back and forth at length.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng also sent a letter to Xijue, arguing back and forth at length.

sentences.zh: 其後並封議遂寢。

translations.literal: Afterward the simultaneous-enfeoffment proposal was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the proposal for simultaneous enfeoffment was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 二十一年京察。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the capital triennial evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year came the capital triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫籥、考功郎中趙南星盡黜執政私人，憲成實左右之。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Sun Gua and Director of Evaluation Zhao Nanxing dismissed all the chief administrators' private clients; Xiancheng was the one who actually guided this.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Sun Gua and Director of Evaluation Zhao Nanxing dismissed all the chief administrators' private clients; Xiancheng was the one who actually guided this.

sentences.zh: 及南星被斥，憲成疏請同罷，不報。

translations.literal: When Nanxing was dismissed, Xiancheng memorialized asking to be dismissed together; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanxing was dismissed, Xiancheng memorialized asking to be dismissed together; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 尋遷文選郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to director of the Civil Office section.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to director of the Civil Office section.

sentences.zh: 所推舉率與執政牴牾。

translations.literal: Those he recommended were generally at odds with the chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended were generally at odds with the chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 先是，吏部缺尚書，錫爵欲用羅萬化，憲成不可，乃用陳有年。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister, Xijue wished to appoint Luo Wanhua; Xiancheng opposed it, and Chen Younian was appointed instead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister, Xijue wished to appoint Luo Wanhua; Xiancheng opposed it, and Chen Younian was appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 後廷推閣臣，萬化復不與。

translations.literal: Later, in court nomination for grand secretaries, Wanhua again was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in court nomination for grand secretaries, Wanhua again was not included.

sentences.zh: 錫爵等皆恚，萬化乃獲推，會帝報罷而止。

translations.literal: Xijue and the others were all resentful; Wanhua finally obtained nomination, but when the emperor returned with a dismissal it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue and the others were all resentful; Wanhua finally obtained nomination, but when the emperor returned with a dismissal it stopped.

sentences.zh: 及是，錫爵將謝政，廷推代者。

translations.literal: At this time Xijue was about to resign from government; court nomination chose his replacement.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xijue was about to resign from government; the court nominated his replacement.

sentences.zh: 憲成舉故大學士王家屏，忤帝意，削籍歸。

translations.literal: Xiancheng nominated the former Grand Secretary Wang Jiaoping, which offended the emperor's intent; he was struck from the rolls and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng nominated the former Grand Secretary Wang Jiaoping, which offended the emperor; he was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 事具有年傳。

translations.literal: The matter is treated in full in Younian's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is treated in full in Younian's biography.

sentences.zh: 憲成既廢，名益高，中外推薦無慮百十疏，帝悉不報。

translations.literal: After Xiancheng was dismissed his fame rose ever higher; inside and outside the court, recommendations in memorials numbered easily a hundred or more—but the emperor answered none.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiancheng was dismissed his fame rose ever higher; memorials recommending him from inside and outside the court numbered easily a hundred or more, but the emperor answered none.

sentences.zh: 至三十六年，始起南京光祿少卿，力辭不就。

translations.literal: Only in the thirty-sixth year was he summoned as Vice Director of Ceremonial in Nanjing—but he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the thirty-sixth year was he summoned as Vice Director of Ceremonial in Nanjing, but he firmly declined and did not take office.

sentences.zh: 四十年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢亂政，其黨石三畏追論之，遂削奪。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian threw government into chaos, his faction member Shi Sanwei pursued a review of the case; Xiancheng's honors were then stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian threw government into chaos, his faction member Shi Sanwei pursued a review of the case, and Xiancheng's honors were stripped.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈吏部右侍郎，謚端文。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Duanwen ("Upright in Culture").
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous title Duanwen ("Upright in Culture").

sentences.zh: 憲成姿性絕人，幼即有誌聖學。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's natural gifts surpassed others; even in youth he aspired to the learning of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's natural gifts surpassed others; even in youth he aspired to the learning of the sages.

sentences.zh: 暨削籍裏居，益覃精研究，力辟王守仁「無善無惡心之體」之說。

translations.literal: After he was struck from the rolls and lived in his home district, he studied all the more deeply, and forcefully refuted Wang Shouren's doctrine of "the substance of the mind as neither good nor evil."
translations.idiomatic: After he was struck from the rolls and lived at home, he studied all the more deeply and forcefully refuted Wang Shouren's doctrine of "the substance of the mind as neither good nor evil."

sentences.zh: 邑故有東林書院，宋楊時講道處也，憲成與弟允成倡修之，常州知府歐陽東鳳與無錫知縣林宰為之營構。

translations.literal: In the district there was originally the Donglin Academy, the place where Yang Shi of the Song lectured on the Way; Xiancheng together with his younger brother Yuncheng led the effort to restore it, and Ouyang Dongfeng, prefect of Changzhou, and Lin Zai, magistrate of Wuxi, saw to its construction.
translations.idiomatic: The district already had the Donglin Academy, where Yang Shi of the Song had lectured on the Way; Xiancheng and his younger brother Yuncheng led a campaign to restore it, while Ouyang Dongfeng, prefect of Changzhou, and Lin Zai, magistrate of Wuxi, arranged the building work.

sentences.zh: 落成，偕同誌高攀龍、錢一本、薛敷教、史孟麟、於孔兼輩講學其中，學者稱涇陽先生。

translations.literal: When it was completed, he joined like-minded men—Gao Panlong, Qian Yiben, Xue Fujiao, Shi Menglin, Yu Kongjian, and others—in lecturing there; scholars called him Master Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, he lectured there with kindred spirits—Gao Panlong, Qian Yiben, Xue Fujiao, Shi Menglin, Yu Kongjian, and others—and scholars called him Master Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 當是時，士大夫抱道忤時者，率退處林野，聞風響附，學舍至不能容。

translations.literal: At that time, scholar-officials who embraced the Way but offended the times generally withdrew to forests and fields; hearing the wind they rallied to him, and the academy could hardly hold them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time scholar-officials who held to the Way yet clashed with the times mostly retired to the countryside; drawn by his reputation they flocked to him until the academy could no longer hold them.

sentences.zh: 憲成嘗曰：「官輦轂，誌不在君父，官封疆，誌不在民生，居水邊林下，誌不在世道，君子無取焉。」

translations.literal: Xiancheng once said: "If one serves at the imperial carriage-hub yet his will is not set on lord and father, if one serves on the frontiers yet his will is not set on the people's livelihood, if one dwells by rivers and in forests yet his will is not set on the way of the age—a gentleman should have nothing to do with such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng once said: "Serving at the capital yet caring nothing for sovereign and father, serving on the frontier yet caring nothing for the people's livelihood, living in seclusion by rivers and woods yet caring nothing for the fate of the age—such a man is no gentleman worth the name.

sentences.zh: 故其講習之余，往往諷議朝政，裁量人物。

translations.literal: Therefore, beyond their lectures and study, they often offered indirect criticism of court policy and passed judgment on public figures.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, when they were not lecturing they often offered veiled criticism of court policy and passed judgment on public figures.

sentences.zh: 朝士慕其風者，多遙相應和。

translations.literal: Court officials who admired their ethos often answered from afar in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials who admired their spirit often echoed them from afar.

sentences.zh: 由是東林名大著，而忌者亦多。

translations.literal: Thus the name of Donglin grew greatly renowned, and those who envied them grew numerous as well.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Donglin's fame spread far and wide, and those who resented it grew numerous as well.

sentences.zh: 既而淮撫李三才被論，憲成貽書葉向高、孫丕揚為延譽。

translations.literal: Before long the Huai commissioner Li Sancai came under attack; Xiancheng sent letters to Ye Xianggao and Sun Piyang to speak well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Huai commissioner Li Sancai came under attack; Xiancheng wrote to Ye Xianggao and Sun Piyang asking them to speak on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 御史吳亮刻之邸抄中，攻三才者大嘩。

translations.literal: The censor Wu Liang had them printed in the Court Gazette; those attacking Sancai erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Wu Liang had the letters printed in the Court Gazette, and those attacking Sancai erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 而其時於玉立、黃正賓輩附麗其間，頗有輕浮好事名。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Yu Yuli, Huang Zhengbin, and others attached themselves to the circle and gained some reputation for frivolity and meddling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time Yu Yuli, Huang Zhengbin, and others hung about the group and acquired a reputation for frivolity and stirring up trouble.

sentences.zh: 徐兆魁之徒遂以東林為口實。

translations.literal: Men like Xu Zhaokui then took Donglin as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xu Zhaokui then seized on Donglin as a pretext for attack.

sentences.zh: 兆魁騰疏攻憲成，恣意誣詆。

translations.literal: Zhaokui sent up a memorial attacking Xiancheng, freely slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaokui sent up a memorial attacking Xiancheng, slandering him at will.

sentences.zh: 謂滸墅有小河，東林專其稅為書院費；

translations.literal: He alleged that at Huxu there was a small river whose tolls Donglin monopolized for academy expenses;
translations.idiomatic: He claimed that at Huxu a small river's tolls were monopolized by Donglin to fund the academy;

sentences.zh: 關使至，東林輒以書招之，即不赴，亦必致厚饋；

translations.literal: when transit commissioners arrived Donglin would invite them by letter, and even if they did not come they still sent lavish gifts;
translations.idiomatic: whenever transit commissioners arrived Donglin would summon them by letter, and even if they did not come they were still sent lavish gifts;

sentences.zh: 講學所至，仆從如雲，縣令館谷供億，非二百金不辦；

translations.literal: wherever they lectured, attendants thronged like clouds and county magistrates had to lodge and supply them at no less than two hundred taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: wherever they lectured attendants swarmed like clouds, and county magistrates had to lodge and provision them at a cost of no less than two hundred taels;

sentences.zh: 會時必談時政，郡邑行事偶相左，必令改圖；

translations.literal: at gatherings they always discussed current politics, and if a prefecture or county acted contrary to their views they insisted on a change of plan;
translations.idiomatic: at their meetings they always discussed current politics, and if a prefecture or county did something they disliked they demanded a change of course;

sentences.zh: 及受黃正賓賄。

translations.literal: and that Xiancheng had accepted bribes from Huang Zhengbin.
translations.idiomatic: and that Xiancheng had taken bribes from Huang Zhengbin.

sentences.zh: 其言絕無左驗。

translations.literal: None of these charges had any corroboration whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Not one of these charges had any corroboration at all.

sentences.zh: 光祿丞吳炯上言為一致辨，因言：「憲成貽書救三才，誠為出位，臣嘗咎之，憲成亦自悔。

translations.literal: Wu Jiong, Vice Director of Ceremonial, memorialized in his defense, saying: "Xiancheng's letters pleading for Sancai were indeed overstepping; I once reproached him for it, and Xiancheng himself has regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jiong, Vice Director of Ceremonial, memorialized in his defense, saying: "Xiancheng's letters pleading for Sancai were indeed overstepping; I once reproached him for it, and Xiancheng himself has regretted it.

sentences.zh: 今憲成被誣，天下將以講學為戒，絕口不談孔、孟之道，國家正氣從此而損，非細事也。」

translations.literal: Now that Xiancheng is slandered, the empire will take lecturing as a warning and fall silent on the Way of Confucius and Mencius—the state's vital spirit will suffer from this; it is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Xiancheng is slandered, the empire will treat lecturing as a warning and fall silent on the Way of Confucius and Mencius—the state's vital spirit will be damaged by this, and it is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 嗣後攻擊者不絕，比憲成歿，攻者猶未止。

translations.literal: Thereafter attacks did not cease; by the time Xiancheng died the assailants had still not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the attacks never let up; even after Xiancheng died the assailants had not stopped.

sentences.zh: 凡救三才者，爭辛亥京察者，衛國本者，發韓敬科場弊者，請行勘熊廷弼者，抗論張差梃擊者，最後爭移宮、紅丸者，忤魏忠賢者，率指目為東林，抨擊無虛日。

translations.literal: Those who defended Sancai, who fought over the Xinsi capital evaluation, who guarded the foundation of the state, who exposed Han Jing's examination abuses, who requested investigation of Xiong Tingbi, who debated Zhang Cha's club assault, who finally fought over the palace transfer and the Red Pill, and who offended Wei Zhongxian—all were pointed at as Donglin, and attacks came day after day without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had defended Sancai, fought over the Xinsi capital evaluation, upheld the heir apparent, exposed Han Jing's examination scandal, called for an inquiry into Xiong Tingbi, argued over Zhang Cha's club assault, and finally contested the palace transfer and the Red Pill case, along with anyone who crossed Wei Zhongxian—all were fingered as Donglin, and the attacks never ceased for a single day.

sentences.zh: 借魏忠賢毒焰，一網盡去之。

translations.literal: Borrowing Wei Zhongxian's poisonous power, they swept them all away in one net.
translations.idiomatic: Riding Wei Zhongxian's poisonous power, they swept them all away in one net.

sentences.zh: 殺戮禁錮，善類為一空。

translations.literal: Killings and imprisonments left the ranks of the good utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: Through slaughter and imprisonment the ranks of the worthy were emptied.

sentences.zh: 崇禎立，始漸收用。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen ascended the throne they were gradually brought back into service.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen took the throne they were gradually brought back into office.

sentences.zh: 而朋黨勢已成，小人卒大熾，禍中於國，迄明亡而後已。

translations.literal: But factional power was already set; petty men ultimately flourished greatly, misfortune struck the state, and did not end until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: But factional power was already entrenched; petty men ultimately flourished, disaster struck the state, and did not end until the Ming fell.

sentences.zh: 歐陽東鳳，字千仞，潛江人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Dongfeng, styled Qianren, was a native of Qianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Dongfeng, styled Qianren, was a native of Qianjiang.

sentences.zh: 年十四喪父，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: At fourteen he lost his father; grief wore him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he lost his father; grief wore him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 母病嘔血，跪而食之。

translations.literal: When his mother was ill and vomited blood, he knelt and ate it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was ill and vomited blood, he knelt and ate it himself.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，縣令憫其貧，遺以田二百畝，謝不受。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination; the county magistrate, pitying his poverty, gave him two hundred mou of fields, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination; the county magistrate, pitying his poverty, gave him two hundred mou of land, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年成進士，除興化知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 大水壞堤，請振於上官不應，遂自疏於朝。

translations.literal: Great floods breached the dikes; he requested relief from his superiors but got no answer, so he memorialized the court directly.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods destroyed the dikes; he requested relief from his superiors but received no answer, so he memorialized the court directly.

sentences.zh: 坐越奏停俸，然竟如所請。

translations.literal: He was penalized for overstepping with a memorial and had his salary suspended, yet in the end his request was granted as asked.
translations.idiomatic: He was penalized for overstepping authority with his memorial and had his salary suspended, yet in the end he obtained what he had asked for.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京刑部郎中，擢平樂知府。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments, then was promoted to prefect of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments, then was promoted to prefect of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 撫諭生瑤，皆相親如子弟。

translations.literal: He pacified and instructed the uncultivated Yao, who all treated one another as close as sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified and instructed the raw Yao, who all grew as close as sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 因白督學監司，擇其俊秀者入學，瑤漸知禮讓。

translations.literal: He reported to the educational commissioner and overseers to select their talented youth for the schools, and the Yao gradually learned ritual and deference.
translations.idiomatic: He informed the educational commissioner and overseers, who selected their promising youth for the schools, and the Yao gradually learned ritual and deference.

sentences.zh: 稅使橫行，東鳳力抗之。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners ran rampant; Dongfeng strenuously resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioners ran rampant, and Dongfeng resisted them strenuously.

sentences.zh: 以才調常州。

translations.literal: For his ability he was transferred to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his ability he was transferred to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 布帷瓦器，胥吏不能牟一錢，擒奸人劇盜且盡。

translations.literal: He used cloth curtains and earthenware; clerks could not squeeze a single cash, and he captured rogues and major bandits nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: He used cloth curtains and earthenware vessels; clerks could not extort a single cash, and he captured scoundrels and major bandits almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 憲成輩講學，為建東林書院。

translations.literal: When Xiancheng and his fellows lectured, he built the Donglin Academy for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng and his circle lectured, he built the Donglin Academy for them.

sentences.zh: 居四年，謝事歸。

translations.literal: After four years he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起山西副使，擢南京太仆少卿，並辭不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Commissioner in Shanxi and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing, but declined both and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Commissioner in Shanxi and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing, but declined both posts and did not take office.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 吳炯，字晉明，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Wu Jiong, styled Jinming, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jiong, styled Jinming, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年成進士，授杭州推官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating censor of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部主事，乞假歸。

translations.literal: He entered the Ministry of War as a director, then asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of War as a director, then asked for leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 恬靜端介，不騖榮利。

translations.literal: Calm, upright, and self-contained, he did not chase glory or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Calm, upright, and reserved, he did not chase rank or profit.

sentences.zh: 家居十二年，始起故官。

translations.literal: At home twelve years, he was only then restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home twelve years before he was finally restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 久之，進光祿丞。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was advanced to Vice Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to Vice Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，累遷南京太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he rose by stages to Director of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he rose by stages to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢私人石三畏追論炯黨庇憲成，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian's partisan Shi Sanwei pursued a case against Jiong for factional protection of Xiancheng; he was removed from office and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's partisan Shi Sanwei pursued a case against Jiong for shielding Xiancheng as a factional ally; he was dismissed and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 炯家世素封，無子，置義田以贍族人。

translations.literal: Jiong's family had long been wealthy; having no son, he set aside charitable fields to support his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's family had long been wealthy; having no son, he set aside charitable fields to support his clansmen.

sentences.zh: 郡中貧士及諸生赴舉者，多所資給。

translations.literal: He gave generously to poor scholars in the commandery and to students traveling to examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He gave generously to poor scholars in the prefecture and to students traveling to take the examinations.

sentences.zh: 嘗輸萬金助邊，被詔旌獎。

translations.literal: He once contributed ten thousand taels to aid the frontier and was honored by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: He once contributed ten thousand taels to aid the frontier and was honored by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 顧允成，字季時，憲成弟。

translations.literal: Gu Yuncheng, styled Jishi, was Xiancheng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yuncheng, styled Jishi, was Xiancheng's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 性耿介，厲名節，舉萬歷十一年會試，十四年始赴殿試。

translations.literal: By nature stern and upright, he prized moral integrity; he passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of Wanli and only in the fourteenth year presented himself for the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: By nature stern and upright, he prized moral integrity; he passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of Wanli and only in the fourteenth year sat for the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 對策中有曰：「陛下以鄭妃勤於奉侍，冊為皇貴妃，廷臣不勝私憂過計。

translations.literal: In his examination response he said: "Your Majesty, because Consort Zheng was diligent in attendance, enfeoffed her as Imperial Noble Consort—the court officials could not overcome private anxiety and excessive foreboding.
translations.idiomatic: In his examination response he wrote: "Your Majesty, because Consort Zheng was diligent in attendance, enfeoffed her as Imperial Noble Consort—the court officials could not help private anxiety and excessive worry.

sentences.zh: 請立東宮，進封王恭妃，非報罷則峻逐。

translations.literal: In urging the establishment of the Eastern Palace and advancing Lady Wang the Respectful Consort, if they were not answered with dismissal they were harshly expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Those who urged establishing the Eastern Palace and advancing Lady Wang the Respectful Consort were either dismissed with no answer or harshly driven out.

sentences.zh: 或不幸貴妃弄威福，其戚屬左右竊而張之，內外害可勝言！

translations.literal: If by misfortune the noble consort wielded power and favor, and her kin and attendants stole and spread it abroad—the harm inside and outside could hardly be told!
translations.idiomatic: If by misfortune the noble consort wielded power and favor, and her kin and attendants stole authority and spread it abroad—the harm inside and outside defies description!

sentences.zh: 頃張居正罔上行私，陛下以為不足信，而付之二三匪人。

translations.literal: Recently Zhang Juzheng deceived his lord and pursued private ends; Your Majesty judged him not worth trusting, yet entrusted affairs to two or three unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zhang Juzheng deceived his lord and pursued private ends; Your Majesty judged him unworthy of trust, yet entrusted affairs to two or three unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 恐居正之專，尚與陛下二。

translations.literal: I fear that Juzheng's monopoly still left two parties with Your Majesty—
translations.idiomatic: I fear that under Juzheng's monopoly Your Majesty still had a counterweight—

sentences.zh: 此屬之專，遂與陛下一。

translations.literal: whereas this lot's monopoly makes them one with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: whereas this lot's monopoly makes them one with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 二則易間，一難圖也。」

translations.literal: When there are two, wedges are easy; when there is one, plotting is hard.
translations.idiomatic: When there are two, wedges are easy; when there is one, plotting is hard.

sentences.zh: 執政駭且恚，置末第。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were alarmed and resentful; he was placed in the last rank.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were alarmed and furious; he was placed in the last rank.

sentences.zh: 會南畿督學御史德清人房寰連疏詆都御史海瑞，允成不勝憤。

translations.literal: It happened that Fang Huan of Deqing, educational inspector of the southern metropolitan region, sent repeated memorials slandering the censor-in-chief Hai Rui; Yuncheng could not contain his rage.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Fang Huan of Deqing, educational inspector of the southern metropolitan region, sent repeated memorials slandering the censor-in-chief Hai Rui; Yuncheng could not contain his anger.

sentences.zh: 偕同年生彭遵古、諸壽賢抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: Together with his year-mates Peng Zungu and Zhu Shouxian he submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his year-mates Peng Zungu and Zhu Shouxian he submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 略言：「寰妒賢醜正，不復知人間羞耽事。

translations.literal: It said in part: "Huan envies the worthy and defames the upright; he no longer knows the meaning of shame in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It said in part: "Huan envies the worthy and defames the upright; he no longer knows what shame means among human beings.

sentences.zh: 臣等自幼讀書，即知慕瑞，以為當代偉人。

translations.literal: We have read books since youth and knew to admire Rui, holding him a great man of the age.
translations.idiomatic: We have read books since childhood and admired Rui, holding him a great man of the age.

sentences.zh: 寰大肆貪汙，聞瑞之風，宜愧且死，反敢造言逞誣，臣等所為痛心。」

translations.literal: Huan is flagrantly corrupt; hearing of Rui's example he ought to die of shame, yet he dares fabricate words and vent slander—this is what rends our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Huan is flagrantly corrupt; hearing of Rui's example he ought to die of shame, yet he dares fabricate charges and vent slander—this is what breaks our hearts.

sentences.zh: 因劾其欺罔七罪。

translations.literal: They therefore impeached him on seven counts of deceit.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore impeached him on seven counts of deceit.

sentences.zh: 始寰疏出，朝野多切齒。

translations.literal: When Huan's memorials first appeared, court and country mostly gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan's memorials first appeared, court and country gnashed their teeth in anger.

sentences.zh: 而政府庇之，但擬旨譙讓。

translations.literal: But the government sheltered him and only drafted an edict of reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: But the government sheltered him and only drafted an edict of reprimand.

sentences.zh: 及得允成等疏，謂寰已切讓，不當出位妄奏，奪三人冠帶，還家省愆，且令九卿約束辦事進士，毋妄言時政。

translations.literal: When Yuncheng's memorial arrived they said Huan had already been sharply reprimanded and that others must not overstep with reckless memorials; the three men's caps and girdles were taken, they were sent home to reflect on faults, and the Nine Ministers were ordered to restrain duty-assigned jinshi from rashly discussing current politics.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuncheng's memorial arrived they said Huan had already been sharply reprimanded and that others must not overstep with reckless memorials; the three men's caps and girdles were taken, they were sent home to reflect on their faults, and the Nine Ministers were ordered to restrain jinshi on probationary duty from rashly discussing current politics.

sentences.zh: 南京太仆卿沈思孝上言：「二三年來，今日以建言防人，明日以越職加人罪，且移牒諸司約禁，而進士觀政者，復令堂官鉗束之。

translations.literal: Shen Sixiao, Director of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing, memorialized: "For two or three years now, today one is barred for speaking out, tomorrow another is punished for overstepping his office; edicts of restraint go out to every agency, and jinshi observing government are again ordered restrained by their department heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Sixiao, Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing, memorialized: "For two or three years now, today someone is blocked for speaking out, tomorrow someone is punished for overstepping his office; restraining edicts go out to every agency, and jinshi observing government are again ordered restrained by their department heads.

sentences.zh: 夫禁其作奸犯科可也，而反禁其讜言直諫；

translations.literal: One may forbid wrongdoing and crime, yet one forbids loyal remonstrance instead;
translations.idiomatic: Wrongdoing and crime may be forbidden, yet loyal remonstrance is forbidden instead;

sentences.zh: 教其砥行立節可也，而反教以緘默取容。

translations.literal: one may teach upright conduct and moral integrity, yet one teaches silence and ingratiation instead.
translations.idiomatic: upright conduct and moral integrity may be taught, yet silence and ingratiation are taught instead.

sentences.zh: 此風一開，流弊何極。

translations.literal: Once this wind opens, how far will the harm flow?
translations.idiomatic: Once this wind takes hold, how far will the harm run?

sentences.zh: 諫官避禍希寵不言矣，庶官又不當言；

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials avoid calamity and court favor by not speaking, yet ordinary officials must not speak either;
translations.idiomatic: Censors avoid disaster and court favor by keeping silent, yet ordinary officials must not speak either;

sentences.zh: 大臣持祿養交不言矣，小臣又不許言。

translations.literal: great ministers hold their salaries and cultivate connections by not speaking, yet junior officials are not allowed to speak either.
translations.idiomatic: great ministers hold their salaries and cultivate connections by keeping silent, yet junior officials are not allowed to speak either.

sentences.zh: 萬一權奸擅朝，傾危宗社，陛下安從聞之？

translations.literal: If by chance powerful traitors monopolized the court and endangered the altars of state—how would Your Majesty hear of it?
translations.idiomatic: If by chance powerful traitors seized the court and endangered the altars of state, how would Your Majesty hear of it?

sentences.zh: 臣歷稽先朝故事，練綱、鄒智、孫磐、張璁並以書生建言，未聞以為罪，獨奈何錮允成等耶？」

translations.literal: I have traced precedents in former reigns: Lian Gang, Zou Zhi, Sun Pan, and Zhang Cong all spoke as mere scholars, and were not treated as criminal—why alone imprison Yuncheng and the others?
translations.idiomatic: I have traced precedents in former reigns: Lian Gang, Zou Zhi, Sun Pan, and Zhang Cong all spoke out as mere scholars and were not treated as criminals—why alone punish Yuncheng and the others?

sentences.zh: 疏入，忤旨被責，三人遂廢。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; offending the intent he was rebuked, and the three were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; offending the throne he was rebuked, and the three were ruined.

sentences.zh: 寰復詆瑞及思孝，其言絕狂誕，自是獲罪清議，出為江西副使。

translations.literal: Huan again slandered Rui and Sixiao in language utterly wild and absurd; from this he earned the condemnation of pure criticism and was sent out as Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan again slandered Rui and Sixiao in language utterly wild and absurd; from this he earned the condemnation of upright opinion and was sent out as Vice Commissioner in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 給事中張鼎思劾其奸貪，寰亦訐鼎思請寄事。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhang Dingsi impeached him for corruption and wickedness; Huan in turn accused Dingsi of soliciting favors.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zhang Dingsi impeached him for corruption and wickedness; Huan in turn accused Dingsi of soliciting favors.

sentences.zh: 諸給事中不平，連章攻寰，寰與鼎思並謫，遂不復振。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries were indignant and attacked Huan in linked memorials; Huan and Dingsi were both demoted and never recovered their standing.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries were indignant and attacked Huan in a series of memorials; Huan and Dingsi were both demoted and never recovered their standing.

sentences.zh: 久之，南京御史陳邦科請錄用允成等，不許。

translations.literal: After a long time the Nanjing censor Chen Bangke requested that Yuncheng and others be reemployed; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval the Nanjing censor Chen Bangke requested that Yuncheng and others be reemployed; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史復言之，詔許以教授用。

translations.literal: The touring inspector censor spoke again; an edict permitted their use as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor spoke again; an edict permitted their appointment as instructors.

sentences.zh: 允成歷任南康、保定。

translations.literal: Yuncheng served in succession at Nankang and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng served in succession at Nankang and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監博士，遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: He entered as Doctor of the Directorate of Education and was transferred to a director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a doctor of the Directorate of Education and was transferred to a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 三王並封制下，偕同官張納陛、工部主事嶽元聲合疏諫曰：「冊立大典，年來無敢再瀆者，以奉二十一年舉行之明詔。

translations.literal: When the decree for enfeoffing the three princes together was issued, he joined his colleague Zhang Nabi and Yue Yuansheng, a director in the Ministry of Works, in a joint remonstrance saying: "The great ceremony of investiture of the heir—for years none dared again profane it, in obedience to the clear edict of twenty-one years past that it be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree enfeoffing the three princes together was issued, he joined his colleague Zhang Nabi and Yue Yuansheng, a director in the Ministry of Works, in a joint remonstrance saying: "The great ceremony of investiture of the heir—for years none dared profane it again, in obedience to the clear edict of twenty-one years ago that it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 茲既屆期，群臣莫不引領。

translations.literal: Now that the term has arrived, the ministers all crane their necks in expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the appointed time has arrived, the ministers all wait with eager expectation.

sentences.zh: 而元輔王錫爵星駕趣朝，一見禮部尚書羅萬化、儀制郎於孔兼，即戒之弗言，慨然獨任，臣等實喜且慰。

translations.literal: Yet the Senior Grand Secretary Wang Xijue traveled night and day to court; at one meeting with the Minister of Rites Luo Wanhua and the Bureau Director Yu Kongjian he warned them not to speak, and boldly took sole charge—we were truly glad and relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Senior Grand Secretary Wang Xijue hurried night and day to court; at one meeting with the Minister of Rites Luo Wanhua and the Bureau Director Yu Kongjian he warned them not to speak and boldly took sole charge—we were truly glad and relieved.

sentences.zh: 不意陛下出禁中密劄，竟付錫爵私邸，而三王並封之議遂成，即次輔趙誌臯、張位亦不預聞。

translations.literal: We did not expect Your Majesty to issue a secret missive from the inner palace and deliver it straight to Xijue's private residence, so that the proposal to enfeoff the three princes together took shape, while even the Second Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei were not forewarned.
translations.idiomatic: We did not expect Your Majesty to issue a secret missive from the inner palace and deliver it to Xijue's private residence, so that the proposal to enfeoff the three princes together took shape—even the Second Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei were not forewarned.

sentences.zh: 夫天下事非一家私議。

translations.literal: Surely affairs of the empire are not one family's private deliberation!
translations.idiomatic: Surely affairs of the empire are not one family's private deliberation!

sentences.zh: 元子封王，祖宗以來未有此禮，錫爵安得專之，而陛下安得創之！」

translations.literal: Enfeoffing the eldest son as a prince—no such rite since ancestral times; how could Xijue monopolize it, and how could Your Majesty invent it!
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffing the eldest son as a prince—no such rite since ancestral times; how could Xijue decide it alone, and how could Your Majesty invent it!

sentences.zh: 當是時，光祿丞朱維京、給事中王如堅疏先入。

translations.literal: At that time the memorials of Zhu Weijing, Vice Director of Ceremonial, and the supervising secretary Wang Rujian had already entered first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the memorials of Zhu Weijing, Vice Director of Ceremonial, and the supervising secretary Wang Rujian had already been submitted first.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，戍極邊。

translations.literal: The emperor flew into rage and exiled them to the outermost border.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and exiled them to the remotest frontier.

sentences.zh: 維京同官塗傑、王學曾繼之，斥為民。

translations.literal: Weijing's colleagues in office Tu Jie and Wang Xuezeng followed; they were dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Weijing's colleagues in office Tu Jie and Wang Xuezeng followed suit; they were reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 及是諫者益眾，帝知不可盡斥，但報「遵旨行」。

translations.literal: By then remonstrators grew ever more numerous; the emperor knew they could not all be expelled and only replied, "Carry out as instructed."
translations.idiomatic: By then remonstrators grew ever more numerous; the emperor knew he could not dismiss them all and only replied, "Carry out as instructed."

sentences.zh: 已而竟寢。

translations.literal: Before long it was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the matter was shelved entirely.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吏部尚書孫鑨等以拾遺事被責。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Xuan, Minister of Personnel, and others were reprimanded over the affair of presenting omitted memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sun Xuan, Minister of Personnel, and others were reprimanded over the affair of presenting omitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 允成謂閣臣張位實為之，上疏力詆位，因及錫爵。

translations.literal: Yuncheng held that Grand Secretary Zhang Wei had actually done it; he memorialized forcefully denouncing Wei and by the way implicated Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng held that Grand Secretary Zhang Wei was actually behind it; he memorialized forcefully denouncing Wei and also implicated Xijue.

sentences.zh: 納陛亦抗章極論，並侵附執政者。

translations.literal: Nabi too submitted a defiant memorial arguing to the utmost, and together attacked those attached to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Nabi too submitted a defiant memorial arguing fiercely, jointly attacking those allied with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫允成光州判官，納陛鄧州判官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Yuncheng to magistrate of Guangzhou and Nabi to magistrate of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted Yuncheng to magistrate of Guangzhou and Nabi to magistrate of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 皆乞假歸，不復出。

translations.literal: Both begged leave to return home and never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: Both requested leave to return home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 納陛，字以登，宜興人。

translations.literal: Nabi, styled Yideng, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Nabi, styled Yideng, was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 年十六，從王畿講學。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he followed Wang Ji in lecturing and study.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he studied under Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 由刑部主事改禮部。

translations.literal: From a director in the Ministry of Punishments he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred from a directorship in the Ministry of Punishments to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 生平尚風節。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he prized integrity of character.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he prized moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 鄉邑有利害，輒為請於有司而後已。

translations.literal: When his home district had matters of benefit or harm, he would always plead with the authorities on its behalf before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When matters of public benefit or harm arose in his home district, he always pleaded with the authorities on its behalf before resting.

sentences.zh: 東林書院之會，納陛為焉。

translations.literal: At the gatherings of the Donglin Academy, Nabi was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Nabi took part in the gatherings of the Donglin Academy.

sentences.zh: 又與同邑史孟麟、吳正誌為麗澤大會，東南人士爭赴之。

translations.literal: Again with his fellow-townsman Shi Menglin and Wu Zhengzhi he held the Great Lizhe Assembly, and men of talent from the southeast vied to attend.
translations.idiomatic: With his fellow townsman Shi Menglin and Wu Zhengzhi he also held the Great Lizhe Assembly, and scholars from the southeast vied to attend.

sentences.zh: 時與允成等同以部曹爭三王並封，又爭拾遺事者，戶部主事滁人賈巖，亦貶曹州判官。

translations.literal: At the time, together with Yuncheng and others who as ministry directors had contested the three-princes joint enfeoffment and again contested the presenting-of-omissions affair, Jia Yan of Chuzhou, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, was also demoted to magistrate of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, together with Yuncheng and others who as ministry directors had contested the joint enfeoffment of the three princes and the affair of presenting omitted memorials, Jia Yan of Chuzhou, a director in the Ministry of Revenue, was also demoted to magistrate of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 投劾歸，卒。

translations.literal: He submitted his resignation and returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈允成、納陛光祿少卿，巖尚寶丞。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign Yuncheng and Nabi were posthumously granted Vice Director of Ceremonial, and Yan Vice Director of the Imperial Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign Yuncheng and Nabi were posthumously granted Vice Director of Ceremonial, and Yan Vice Director of the Imperial Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 諸壽賢，字延之，昆山人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shouxian, styled Yanzhi, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouxian, styled Yanzhi, was a native of Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 既釋褐，上疏願放歸田，力學十年，然後從政。

translations.literal: Having left sackcloth, he memorialized asking to be released to the fields, to study with effort ten years, and then enter government.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first taking office he memorialized asking to be released to his fields, to study diligently for ten years, and only then enter government service.

sentences.zh: 章下所司，寢不奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the relevant office and shelved without being presented.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant office and shelved without being forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既斥歸。

translations.literal: Having been dismissed he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起南陽教授。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was summoned as instructor at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned as instructor at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 入為國子助教，擢禮部主事。

translations.literal: He entered as assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education and was promoted to a director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education and was promoted to a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 戚里中貴幹請，輒拒之。

translations.literal: When relatives of the empress and powerful eunuchs made requests through connections, he always refused them.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives of the empress and powerful eunuchs sought favors through connections, he always refused.

sentences.zh: 遘疾，請告歸，授徒自給。

translations.literal: Struck by illness, he requested leave to return home and supported himself by teaching pupils.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by illness, he requested leave to return home and supported himself by teaching students.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long interval he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he died.

sentences.zh: 彭遵古，麻城人，終光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Peng Zungu, a native of Macheng, ended as Vice Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zungu, a native of Macheng, rose to Vice Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 錢一本，字國瑞，武進人。

translations.literal: Qian Yiben, styled Guorui, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yiben, styled Guorui, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 除廬陵知縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Luling and summoned to be appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Luling and then summoned as censor.

sentences.zh: 入臺即發原任江西巡按祝大舟貪墨狀，大舟至遣戍。

translations.literal: Upon entering the Censorate he immediately exposed the corruption of Zhu Dazhou, his former predecessor as touring inspector of Jiangxi; Dazhou was sent to frontier exile.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the Censorate he immediately exposed the corruption of Zhu Dazhou, the former touring inspector of Jiangxi; Dazhou was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 已，論請從祀曹端、陳真晟、羅倫、羅洪先於文廟。

translations.literal: Then he argued requesting that Cao Duan, Chen Zhensheng, Luo Lun, and Luo Hongxian be admitted to sacrifice in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: He then argued that Cao Duan, Chen Zhensheng, Luo Lun, and Luo Hongxian should be admitted to sacrifice in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 出按廣西。

translations.literal: He went out as touring inspector of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched as touring inspector of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 帝以張有德請備大禮儀物，復更冊立東宮期，而申時行柄國，不能匡救。

translations.literal: Because Zhang Youde requested provisions for the Grand Rites ceremonial objects, the emperor again changed the term for investiture of the Eastern Palace, while Shen Shihang held state power and could not rectify and save.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang Youde requested provisions for the Grand Rites ceremonial objects, the emperor again postponed the date for investing the Eastern Palace heir, while Shen Shihang held power and could not set matters right.

sentences.zh: 一本上論相、建儲二疏。

translations.literal: Yiben submitted two memorials, on the chief minister and on establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yiben submitted two memorials, one on the chief minister and one on establishing the heir.

sentences.zh: 其論相曰：

translations.literal: On the chief minister he said:
translations.idiomatic: On the chief minister he wrote:

sentences.zh: 昨俞旨下輔臣，令輔臣總政。

translations.literal: Yesterday an imperial assent was issued to the assisting ministers, ordering the assisting ministers to oversee government altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday an imperial directive was issued to the assisting ministers, ordering them to oversee all government affairs.

sentences.zh: 夫朝廷之政，輔臣安得總之？

translations.literal: How can the assisting ministers wholly oversee the government of the court?
translations.idiomatic: How can the assisting ministers wholly control the government of the court?

sentences.zh: 內閣代言擬旨，本顧問之遺，遇有章奏，閣臣宜各擬一旨。

translations.literal: The Inner Secretariat speaks for others and drafts rescripts, originally the remnant of advisory duty; when memorials arrive, each Grand Secretary ought to draft one rescript each.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Secretariat speaks for the throne and drafts rescripts, originally a remnant of advisory duty; when memorials arrive, each Grand Secretary ought to draft a rescript of his own.

sentences.zh: 今一出時行專斷。

translations.literal: Now it all issues from Shihang's sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: Now every rescript issues from Shihang alone.

sentences.zh: 皇上斷者十一，時行斷者十九。

translations.literal: His Majesty decided one in eleven; Shihang decided nineteen in twenty.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty decided one case in eleven; Shihang decided nineteen in twenty.

sentences.zh: 皇上斷謂之聖旨，時行斷亦謂之聖旨。

translations.literal: His Majesty's decisions are called holy edicts; Shihang's decisions are also called holy edicts.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty's decisions are called imperial edicts; Shihang's decisions are also called imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 惟嫌怨所在，則以出自聖斷為言，罪何可勝誅。

translations.literal: Only where there is hatred does one speak of it as issuing from the sacred decision—how can offences be exhaustively punished!
translations.idiomatic: Only where there is personal enmity does one invoke the sacred decision—how can guilt ever be fully punished!

sentences.zh: 所當論者一。

translations.literal: This is the first matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 評事雒於仁進四藥之箴，陛下欲見之施行，輔臣力勸留中。

translations.literal: The reviewer Luo Yuren presented a remonstrance on the four medicines; Your Majesty wished to see it carried out, but the assisting ministers strongly urged keeping it withheld at court.
translations.idiomatic: The reviewer Luo Yuren presented a remonstrance on the four medicines; Your Majesty wished to see it carried out, but the assisting ministers strongly urged withholding it at court.

sentences.zh: 既有言及輔臣之章，亦盡留中不下。

translations.literal: Memorials that spoke of the assisting ministers were also all kept withheld at court and not sent down.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials criticizing the assisting ministers were also all withheld at court and never forwarded.

sentences.zh: 道吾君以遂非文過如此，復安望其盡忠補過耶？

translations.literal: To guide our lord so he persists in wrong and papers over faults in this way—how can one still hope they will exhaust loyalty and remedy faults!
translations.idiomatic: To guide our lord to persist in wrong and paper over faults in this way—how can one still hope they will serve with full loyalty and remedy those faults!

sentences.zh: 所當論者二。

translations.literal: This is the second matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 科場弊竇，汙人齒頰，而敢擬原無私弊之旨，以欺吾君。

translations.literal: The corrupt holes of the examination field stain men's lips and cheeks, yet they dare draft a rescript saying originally there was no private corruption, to deceive our lord.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption in the examination halls is notorious, yet they dare draft a rescript claiming there was no private corruption, to deceive our lord.

sentences.zh: 臣請執政子弟有中式而被人指摘者，除名改蔭。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that sons and younger brothers of those in power who passed the examination and were accused by others be struck from the rolls and have their yin privilege changed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks that sons and younger brothers of those in power who passed the examinations and were accused by others be struck from the rolls and have their hereditary privilege revoked.

sentences.zh: 又與見從仕籍者，暫還裏居，俟父致政，乃議進止。

translations.literal: And those already on the register of active service should temporarily return to their home villages, waiting until their fathers retire from office before deliberating advance or withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: And those already in active service should temporarily return home, waiting until their fathers retire from office before any decision on advancement.

sentences.zh: 毋令犬馬報主之心，不勝其牛馬子孫之計。

translations.literal: Do not let the heart of dogs and horses repaying their master be overcome by the schemes of oxen and horses for their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let loyalty to the throne be overcome by schemes to enrich one's descendants.

sentences.zh: 所當論者三。

translations.literal: This is the third matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 大臣以身殉國，安復有家。

translations.literal: Great ministers offer their persons to die for the state—how can they still have families!
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers devote their lives to the state—how can they still concern themselves with family!

sentences.zh: 乃以遠臣為近臣府庫，又合遠近之臣為內閣府庫。

translations.literal: Yet distant ministers are made the treasury of near ministers, and distant and near ministers together are made the treasury of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet distant officials are made the treasury of near officials, and officials far and near together are made the treasury of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開門受賂自執政始，而歲歲申饋遺之禁何為哉？

translations.literal: Opening the door to receive bribes begins with those in power—so what is the yearly proclamation forbidding gifts for!
translations.idiomatic: Opening the door to bribes begins with those in power—so what is the point of the yearly proclamation forbidding gifts!

sentences.zh: 所當論者四。

translations.literal: This is the fourth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 墨敕斜封，前代所患；

translations.literal: Irregular edicts and slant-sealed appointments were what former ages dreaded;
translations.idiomatic: Irregular edicts and slant-sealed appointments were what former ages dreaded;

sentences.zh: 密啟言事，先臣弗為。

translations.literal: secret memorials on affairs—former ministers did not do this.
translations.idiomatic: secret memorials on state affairs—former ministers did not do this.

sentences.zh: 今閣臣或有救援之舉，或有密勿之謀，類具揭帖以進，雖格言正論，讜議忠謀，已類斜封密啟之為，非有公聽並觀之正。

translations.literal: Now when Grand Secretaries have acts of rescue to urge or secret counsel to offer, they mostly all prepare memorial slips to submit; even upright words and loyal schemes already resemble slant-sealed secret memorials in kind, without the fairness of public hearing and joint viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Now when Grand Secretaries wish to intervene on someone's behalf or offer secret counsel, they mostly submit private memorial slips; even upright words and loyal counsel already resemble slant-sealed secret memorials, without the fairness of open deliberation.

sentences.zh: 況所言公，當與天下公言之；

translations.literal: Moreover what is spoken publicly ought to be spoken publicly to the world;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover what is spoken in public ought to be spoken openly to the world;

sentences.zh: 所言私，忠臣不私。

translations.literal: what is spoken privately, loyal ministers do not keep private.
translations.idiomatic: what is spoken in private, loyal ministers do not keep private.

sentences.zh: 奈何援中書之故事，啟留中之弊端，昭恩怨之所由，示威福之自己。

translations.literal: Why invoke the precedents of the Secretariat, open the abuse of withholding at court, display when favor and hatred arise, and show that power and fortune issue from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Why invoke Secretariat precedents, perpetuate the abuse of withholding memorials at court, reveal the springs of favor and hatred, and show that power and fortune flow from oneself alone.

sentences.zh: 所當論者五。

translations.literal: This is the fifth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 我國家仿古為治，部院即分職之六卿，內閣即論道之三公。

translations.literal: Our state takes antiquity as its model in governing; the ministries and boards are the six ministers with divided duties, the Inner Secretariat is the three dukes who discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Our state takes antiquity as its model in governing; the ministries and boards are the six ministers with divided duties, and the Inner Secretariat is the three dukes who discuss the Way.

sentences.zh: 未聞三公可盡攬六卿之權，歸一人掌握，而六卿又頫首屏氣，唯唯聽命於三公，必為請教而後行也。

translations.literal: One has never heard that the three dukes may wholly seize the authority of the six ministers and concentrate it in one man's grasp, while the six ministers bow their heads, hold their breath, and only yes-yes obey the three dukes, necessarily asking instruction before acting.
translations.idiomatic: One has never heard that the three dukes may seize all the authority of the six ministers and concentrate it in one man's hands, while the six ministers bow their heads, hold their breath, and only murmur assent, necessarily awaiting instruction before acting.

sentences.zh: 所當論者六。

translations.literal: This is the sixth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 三公職在論道。

translations.literal: The three dukes' duty lies in discussing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The three dukes' duty lies in discussing the Way.

sentences.zh: 師，道之教訓。

translations.literal: Teacher—the Way's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Teacher—he who instructs in the Way.

sentences.zh: 今講幄經年不禦，是何師也？

translations.literal: Now the lecture hall has gone years without being attended—what kind of teacher is this?
translations.idiomatic: Now the lecture hall has gone years without an audience—what kind of teacher is this?

sentences.zh: 傅，傅之德義。

translations.literal: Tutor—the tutor's moral meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Tutor—he who tutors in moral principle.

sentences.zh: 今外帑匱乏，私藏充盈，不能一為救正，是何傅也？

translations.literal: Now the outer treasury is exhausted and private stores are full, yet he cannot once set it right—what kind of tutor is this?
translations.idiomatic: Now the public treasury is exhausted while private stores overflow, yet he cannot once set matters right—what kind of tutor is this?

sentences.zh: 保，保其身體。

translations.literal: Guardian—he who guards the body.
translations.idiomatic: Guardian—he who guards the sovereign's person.

sentences.zh: 今聖躬常年靜攝，尚以多疾為辭，是何保也？

translations.literal: Now the sacred person year after year rests in seclusion, still pleading many illnesses as excuse—what kind of guardian is this?
translations.idiomatic: Now His Majesty year after year rests in seclusion, still pleading frequent illness as excuse—what kind of guardian is this?

sentences.zh: 其兼銜必曰太子之師、傅、保，而冊立皇元子之儀，至今又復改遲，臣不知其所兼者何職矣。

translations.literal: Their concurrent titles must say Teacher, Tutor, and Guardian to the Heir Apparent, yet the ceremony of investing the eldest imperial son has again been postponed to a later date—I do not know what office they concurrently hold.
