translations.idiomatic: Their concurrent titles must read Teacher, Tutor, and Guardian to the Heir Apparent, yet the ceremony of investing the eldest imperial son has again been postponed—I do not know what office they concurrently hold.

sentences.zh: 所當論者七。

translations.literal: This is the seventh matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 翰林一途，謂之儲相。

translations.literal: The Hanlin path is called the reserve for chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin path is called the reserve for chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 累貲躡級，循列卿位，以覬必得。

translations.literal: Amassing wealth and treading ranks step by step, following the column to ministerial rank, they look to gain it as a certainty.
translations.idiomatic: Amassing wealth and climbing rank by rank, following the column to ministerial office, they treat high office as a certainty.

sentences.zh: 遂使國家命相之大任，僅為閣臣援引之私物。

translations.literal: Thus the great charge of appointing chief ministers of the state becomes merely a private thing for Grand Secretaries to draw on.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the great charge of appointing the state's chief ministers becomes merely a private resource for Grand Secretaries to dispense.

sentences.zh: 庸者習軟熟結納之態，黠者恣憑陵侵奪之謀。

translations.literal: Mediocre men practice the manner of soft compliance and ingratiating ties; crafty men indulge in bullying and encroaching schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre men practice soft compliance and ingratiating ties; crafty men indulge in bullying and schemes of encroachment.

sentences.zh: 外推內引，珰閣表裏。

translations.literal: Pushing from outside and drawing from within, eunuchs and the Secretariat are inside and outside together.
translations.idiomatic: Pushed from outside and drawn from within, eunuchs and the Secretariat work as one inside and out.

sentences.zh: 始進不正，安望其終？

translations.literal: If the first step is not upright, how can one hope for the end?
translations.idiomatic: If the first step is not upright, how can one hope for a worthy end?

sentences.zh: 故自來內閣之臣一據其位，遠者二十年，近者十年，不敗不止。

translations.literal: Therefore from of old, once Inner Secretariat ministers grasped their posts, the distant lasted twenty years and the near ten, and they did not fall until they could fall no further.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from of old, once Inner Secretariat ministers grasped their posts, the distant lasted twenty years and the near ten, and they did not fall until ruin was complete.

sentences.zh: 嵩之鑒不遠，而居正蹈之；

translations.literal: Yan Song's mirror is not far off, yet Juzheng trod in his tracks;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's lesson is not far off, yet Zhang Juzheng followed in his tracks;

sentences.zh: 居正之鑒不遠，而時行又蹈之。

translations.literal: Juzheng's mirror is not far off, yet Shihang again trod in his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng's lesson is not far off, yet Shihang again followed in his tracks.

sentences.zh: 繼其後者庸碌罷駑，或甚於時行；

translations.literal: Those who follow them are mediocre and worn-out nags, or worse than Shihang;
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow them are mediocre worn-out hacks, or worse than Shihang;

sentences.zh: 褊隘執拗，又復為居正。

translations.literal: narrow-minded and obstinate, they again become Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: narrow-minded and obstinate, they again become another Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 若非大破常格，公天下以選舉，相道終未可言。

translations.literal: Unless the usual norms are greatly broken and the empire is opened to selection for office, the way of the chief minister can never be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the usual norms are greatly broken and selection is opened to the empire, the way of the chief minister can never be restored.

sentences.zh: 所當論者八。

translations.literal: This is the eighth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 先民詢芻蕘之言，明王設誹謗之木。

translations.literal: The ancients sought counsel even in grass and firewood; enlightened kings set up posts for slander.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients sought counsel even from grass and firewood; enlightened kings set up posts for slander.

sentences.zh: 今大臣懼人攻己，而欲鉗天下之口，不目之為奸、為邪、為浮薄，必詈之為讒、為謗、為小人。

translations.literal: Now great ministers fear others attacking themselves and wish to clamp shut the mouths of the empire; unless they call them treacherous, heterodox, or frivolous, they must revile them as slanderers, defamers, or petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Now great ministers fear attack and wish to silence the empire; unless they call critics treacherous, heterodox, or frivolous, they revile them as slanderers, defamers, or petty men.

sentences.zh: 目前之耳目可塗，身後之是非難罔。

translations.literal: Present eyes and ears may be painted over, but right and wrong after death are hard to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Present eyes and ears may be deceived, but posterity's judgment of right and wrong cannot be fooled.

sentences.zh: 所當論者九。

translations.literal: This is the ninth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 君臣之分，等於天地。

translations.literal: The distinction between ruler and minister equals that between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The distinction between ruler and minister equals that between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 今上名之曰總政，己亦居之曰總政。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign names it overseeing government altogether, and he himself also occupies it saying overseeing government altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sovereign names it overseeing all government, and he himself also claims the title of overseeing all government.

sentences.zh: 以其身居於寵利之極，耐彈忍辱，必老死於位而後已。

translations.literal: Because his person occupies the extreme of favor and profit, enduring impeachment and swallowing insult, he must die old in office before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Because he occupies the summit of favor and profit, enduring impeachment and swallowing insult, he must die in office before he will leave.

sentences.zh: 古所謂元老大臣，乃如是其不知進退存亡者耶？

translations.literal: The so-called elder great ministers of antiquity—are they thus ignorant of advance, retreat, survival, and perdition?
translations.idiomatic: Are the so-called elder great ministers of antiquity thus ignorant of when to advance, retreat, survive, or perish?

sentences.zh: 大臣既無難進易退之節，天下安有頑廉懦立之風！

translations.literal: When great ministers lack the integrity of hard to advance and easy to withdraw, how can the empire have the wind of stern integrity and upright standing!
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers lack the integrity to advance with difficulty and withdraw with ease, how can the empire have a climate of stern integrity and upright character!

sentences.zh: 舉一世之人心風俗，糜爛於乞祼登壟之坑，滔滔而莫之止。

translations.literal: To cast the hearts and customs of an entire age into rottenness in the pit of begging at tombs and climbing mounds, rushing on with none to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: To cast the hearts and customs of an entire age into rottenness in the pit of begging at tombs and climbing the mounds of favor, rushing on with none to stop it.

sentences.zh: 是故陛下之治，前數年不勝其操切慘刻，而勢焰爍人；

translations.literal: Therefore under Your Majesty's governance, in the first several years unable to restrain its harsh severity and cruelty, while intimidating authority blazed upon men;
translations.idiomatic: Thus under Your Majesty's governance, in the first years you could not restrain harsh severity and cruelty, while intimidating authority blazed over all;

sentences.zh: 後數年不勝其姑息委靡，而賢愚共貫。

translations.literal: in the later several years unable to restrain its indulgence and enervation, while worthy and foolish were strung together alike.
translations.idiomatic: in later years you could not restrain indulgence and slackness, while worthy and foolish alike were promoted without distinction.

sentences.zh: 前之政自居正總，今之政自時行總，而皆不自朝廷總故也。

translations.literal: The earlier administration was overseen altogether by Juzheng, the present administration is overseen altogether by Shixing—yet neither is overseen altogether from the court for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier administration was run by Zhang Juzheng alone, the present by Shen Shixing alone—yet neither is truly governed from the court at all.

sentences.zh: 所當論者十。

translations.literal: This is the tenth matter that ought to be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth matter that ought to be discussed.

sentences.zh: 然君道莫先論相，而取人亦在君身，願陛下勿以國本為兒戲。

translations.literal: Yet in the Way of the ruler nothing comes before discussing the chief minister, and selecting men lies in the ruler's person as well—your servant prays Your Majesty will not treat the foundation of the state as child's play.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the art of rulership nothing comes before choosing the chief minister, and appointing men depends on the ruler himself—I pray Your Majesty will not treat the succession as a trivial game.

sentences.zh: 昔孔子以九經告君，而先之修身、勸賢。

translations.literal: Formerly Confucius told the ruler with the nine constant principles, yet placed first cultivating the person and encouraging the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius once set forth the nine principles of good government to a ruler, yet placed first self-cultivation and encouraging worthy men.

sentences.zh: 大抵讒夫女謁貨利之交，一有惑溺，則內之心誌決不清明，外之身體決不強固。

translations.literal: Generally speaking, the intersection of slanderers, women's access, and goods and profit—once there is entanglement and drowning, then inward the heart and will absolutely cannot be clear and bright, outward the person and body absolutely cannot be strong and firm.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, once a ruler is entangled with slanderers, palace women's influence, and pursuit of profit, his heart cannot remain clear within nor his resolve firm without.

sentences.zh: 矧以艷處之褒姒，而為善譖之驪姬，狐媚既以蠱其心，鹿臺又復移其誌。

translations.literal: How much more with Baosi of the glamorous dwelling, yet acting as Li Ji skilled in slander—foxlike seduction has already bewitched his heart, and the Stag Tower again has shifted his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when a Baosi in the inner quarters plays Li Ji the slanderer—foxlike seduction has bewitched his heart, and the Stag Tower has shifted his purpose again.

sentences.zh: 陛下之方寸，臣知其不能自持者多矣，抑何以貴德尊士，而修身取人哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's square inch—your servant knows there are many times it cannot hold itself; how then value virtue and honor scholars, and cultivate the person and select men!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart—I know how often it cannot hold firm; how then can you value virtue, honor scholars, cultivate yourself, and choose men wisely!

sentences.zh: 其論國本曰：

translations.literal: His discussion of the foundation of the state said:
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of the succession question read:

sentences.zh: 陛下所以遲遲建儲者，謂欲效皇祖世宗之為耳。

translations.literal: The reason Your Majesty delays establishing the heir is said to be wishing to imitate the conduct of the imperial grandfather Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's reason for delaying the appointment of an heir is said to be a wish to follow the example of the imperial ancestor Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 然皇祖中年嘗立莊敬為太子，封皇考為裕王，非終不立太子也。

translations.literal: Yet the imperial grandfather in mid-life once established Zhuangjing as crown prince and enfeoffed the imperial father as Prince of Yu—he did not in the end refuse to establish a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in mid-life the imperial grandfather did appoint Zhuangjing as crown prince and enfeoffed the imperial father as Prince of Yu—he did not ultimately refuse to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 矧今日事體又迥然不同。

translations.literal: How much more that today's circumstances are again utterly different.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the circumstances today are utterly different.

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃寵過皇后。

translations.literal: The Imperial Noble Consort's favor surpasses the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Noble Consort enjoys favor surpassing that of the empress.

sentences.zh: 其處心積慮，無一日而不萌奪嫡之心，無一日而不思為援立其子之計。

translations.literal: Her brooding heart and accumulated schemes—not one day without sprouting the mind to seize the succession, not one day without thinking to plot establishing her son by support.
translations.idiomatic: In her brooding and schemes, not a day passes without thoughts of displacing the heir, not a day without plotting to establish her own son by outside support.

sentences.zh: 此世宗時所無也。

translations.literal: This was what the Shizong era lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like this existed in the Shizong era.

sentences.zh: 凡子必依於母，皇元子之母壓於皇貴妃之下。

translations.literal: Sons must all depend on their mothers; the mother of the Imperial Eldest Son is pressed beneath the Imperial Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Every son depends on his mother, yet the mother of the Imperial Eldest Son ranks below the Imperial Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 陛下曰「長幼有序」，皇貴妃曰「貴賤有等」。

translations.literal: Your Majesty says, "Elders and juniors have their order"; the Imperial Noble Consort says, "Noble and base have their ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty says, "Elder and younger have their proper order"; the Imperial Noble Consort says, "Noble and humble have their proper ranks."

sentences.zh: 倘一日遂其奪嫡之心，不審陛下何以處此？

translations.literal: If one day she fulfills her mind to seize the succession, your servant does not know how Your Majesty would handle this.
translations.idiomatic: If one day she fulfills her plot to displace the heir, how will Your Majesty handle it?

sentences.zh: 此世宗時所無也。

translations.literal: This was what the Shizong era lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like this existed in the Shizong era.

sentences.zh: 景王就封，止皇考一人在京。

translations.literal: When Prince Jing took up his fief, only the imperial father remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing departed for his fief, only the imperial father remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 今則章服不別，名分不正。

translations.literal: Now robes and regalia are not distinguished, titles and status are not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Now insignia and dress are undistinguished, and titles and status are unclear.

sentences.zh: 弟既憑母之寵而朝夕近幸，母又覬子之立而日夜樹功。

translations.literal: The younger brother already relies on his mother's favor to be near and favored morning and night; the mother again covets her son's installation and day and night builds merit.
translations.idiomatic: The younger prince already relies on his mother's favor for daily access at court; the mother covets his installation and builds his reputation day and night.

sentences.zh: 此世宗時所無也。

translations.literal: This was what the Shizong era lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like this existed in the Shizong era.

sentences.zh: 傳聞陛下先曾失言於皇貴妃，皇貴妃執此為信。

translations.literal: It is rumored Your Majesty once misspoke before the Imperial Noble Consort; the Imperial Noble Consort holds this as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor has it Your Majesty once made an injudicious remark to the Imperial Noble Consort, and she holds it as a pledge.

sentences.zh: 及今不斷，蠱惑日深，剛斷日餒，事體日難。

translations.literal: Until now not severing it, delusion deepens by the day, firm resolution wanes by the day, the affair grows harder by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Because you have not cut this off, her sway deepens daily, your firm resolve weakens daily, and the matter grows harder daily.

sentences.zh: 此世宗時所無也。

translations.literal: This was what the Shizong era lacked.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing like this existed in the Shizong era.

sentences.zh: 前者有旨，不許諸司激擾，愈致遲延，非陛下預設機阱，以禦天下言者乎！

translations.literal: Previously there was an edict forbidding all offices to agitate and provoke, the more to cause delay—is this not Your Majesty's preset trap and snare to ward off all who speak under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Your recent edict forbidding officials from "agitating" the issue only causes further delay—is this not a snare Your Majesty set in advance to silence all who speak under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 使屆期無一人言及，則佯為不知，以冀其遲延。

translations.literal: If when the deadline comes not one person speaks of it, then feign ignorance, hoping for its delay.
translations.idiomatic: If when the deadline arrives no one speaks up, you feign ignorance, hoping for further delay.

sentences.zh: 有一人言及，則禦之曰「此來激擾我也」，改遲一年。

translations.literal: If one person speaks of it, then defend against it saying, "This one comes to agitate and provoke me," and postpone one year.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone speaks up, you rebuff them saying, "They come to agitate me," and postpone another year.

sentences.zh: 明年又一人言及，則又曰「此又來激擾我也」，又改二三年。

translations.literal: Next year again one person speaks of it, then again say, "This one again comes to agitate and provoke me," and again postpone two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, if another speaks up, you say again, "They come to agitate me," and postpone two or three years more.

sentences.zh: 必使天下無一人敢言而後已，庶幾依違遷就，以全其衽席昵愛之私，而曾不顧國本從此動搖，天下從此危亂。

translations.literal: You must bring it about that under Heaven not one person dares speak before stopping, hoping in indecision and accommodation to preserve the private intimacy of bed and pillow, yet never considering that from this the foundation of the state is shaken and under Heaven from this falls into peril and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: You would ensure that no one under Heaven dares speak further, hedging and yielding to preserve your pillow intimacies, never minding that the succession is shaken and the realm thrown into peril.

sentences.zh: 臣以為陛下之禦人至巧，而為謀則甚拙也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that Your Majesty's warding off men is supremely clever, yet in scheming is very clumsy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that Your Majesty is supremely clever at fending off critics, yet very clumsy in counsel.

sentences.zh: 此等機智，不可以罔匹夫匹婦，顧欲以欺天下萬世耶！

translations.literal: Such craft cannot deceive common men and women—yet you would deceive all under Heaven for ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: Such cunning cannot deceive the common man and woman—yet you would deceive all under Heaven for ten thousand generations!

sentences.zh: 疏入，留中。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣相繼爭國本，惟一本言最戇直。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers successively contended over the foundation of the state; only Yiben's words were most blunt and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers were then contending over the succession in succession; only Yiben's words were the bluntest and most direct.

sentences.zh: 帝銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bore a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 無何，杖給事中孟養浩。

translations.literal: Before long, the emperor had the investigating censor Meng Yanghao beaten with the rod.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the investigating censor Meng Yanghao was beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 中旨以養浩所逞之詞根托一本，造言誣君，搖亂大典，遂斥為民。

translations.literal: A rescript from within held that the words Yanghao had vented were rooted in and relied on Yiben—fabricating words to slander the ruler and shaking the great statutes—and he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An inner rescript held that Yanghao's words were rooted in Yiben's influence—fabricating slander against the ruler and shaking the great statutes—and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 屢薦，卒不用。

translations.literal: Yiben was repeatedly recommended, but in the end was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiben was repeatedly recommended but was never employed.

sentences.zh: 一本既罷歸，潛心《六經》濂、洛諸書，尤研精《易》學。

translations.literal: Once Yiben was dismissed and returned home, he immersed his mind in the Six Classics and the books of Lian and Luo, especially penetrating deeply into the learning of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiben was dismissed and returned home, he immersed himself in the Six Classics and the works of the Lian-Luo school, especially the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 與顧憲成輩分主東林講席，學者稱啟新先生。

translations.literal: With Gu Xiancheng and others he presided in turn over the Donglin lecture seat; scholars called him Master Qixin.
translations.idiomatic: With Gu Xiancheng and others he shared leadership of the Donglin lecture platform; scholars called him Master Qixin.

sentences.zh: 裏居二十五年，預克卒日，賦詩誌之，如期而逝。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home twenty-five years, he foretold the day of his death, composed a poem to record it, and passed away on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Living in retirement for twenty-five years, he foretold the day of his death, composed a poem to record it, and died on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈太仆寺少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 子春，字若木，萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: His son Chun, styled Ruomu, passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun, styled Ruomu, passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 32 (1604).

sentences.zh: 歷知高陽、獻二縣，征授御史。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Gaoyang and Xian counties, was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Gaoyang and Xian, then was summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 太仆少卿徐兆魁攻李三才，因痛詆顧憲成。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Xu Zhaokui attacked Li Sancai and in the process bitterly denounced Gu Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Xu Zhaokui attacked Li Sancai and in the process bitterly denounced Gu Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 春三疏首發其憸邪。

translations.literal: Chun in three memorials was first to expose his treacherous wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was first to expose his treachery in three memorials.

sentences.zh: 出按湖廣，請予禮部侍郎郭正域及光祿少卿顧憲成恤典。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Huguang, he requested posthumous honors for Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Gu Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tour in Huguang, he requested posthumous honors for Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu and Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Gu Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 楚宗人以訐偽王事，錮高墻者甚眾，春為訟冤，尋復請釋回故宗家屬，語甚切至。

translations.literal: Chu clansmen because of denouncing the false prince affair—very many were imprisoned in the high wall; Chun pleaded their injustice, and soon again asked to release and return former clansmen's families; his words were very urgent and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Many members of the Chu imperial clan were imprisoned in the high wall after denouncing the false-prince affair; Chun pleaded their cause, and soon asked again for the release of former clansmen's families—his words were urgent and heartfelt.

sentences.zh: 鹹寧知縣滿朝薦久系，奏請釋之，因請並釋王邦才、卞孔時。

translations.literal: Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian had long been imprisoned; he memorialized asking to release him, and by the way asked jointly to release Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning magistrate Man Chaojian had long been imprisoned; Chun memorialized for his release and also for the release of Wang Bangcai and Bian Kongshi.

sentences.zh: 又再疏劾守備中官杜茂，且備陳采榷之害，言：「臣不忍皇上聽小人之謀，名出漢桓、唐德下，為我明基禍之主。」

translations.literal: Again in two memorials he impeached the eunuch defender-in-chief Du Mao, and fully set forth the harm of tax levies and monopolies, saying: "Your servant cannot bear that the emperor listen to petty men's schemes, his name falling below Han Huan and Tang Dezong, becoming a ruler who laid the foundation of calamity for our Great Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He twice more memorialized to impeach the eunuch defender-in-chief Du Mao, fully detailing the harm of tax levies and monopolies, saying: "Your servant cannot bear that Your Majesty heed petty men's schemes, ranking below emperors Huan of Han and Dezong of Tang, becoming a ruler who laid calamity's foundation for our Great Ming.

sentences.zh: 帝以湖廣地為福王莊田。

translations.literal: The emperor took Huguang lands as manor fields for Prince Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had taken Huguang lands as manor estates for Prince Fu.

sentences.zh: 春三疏力爭，帝降旨切責。

translations.literal: Chun in three memorials strove bitterly against it; the emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Chun contested this forcefully in three memorials; the emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 葉向高致政去，方從哲為首輔。

translations.literal: Ye Xianggao retired from office and departed; Fang Congzhe became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao retired from office; Fang Congzhe became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 春抗疏言：「今天下人材則朝虛野實，貨財則野虛朝實。

translations.literal: Chun submitted a defiant memorial saying: "Today under Heaven in talent the court is empty and the countryside full, in goods and wealth the countryside empty and the court full.
translations.idiomatic: Chun submitted a defiant memorial saying: "Today talent is scarce at court but abundant in the countryside; wealth is scarce in the countryside but abundant at court.

sentences.zh: 從哲不能救正，而第於福王則無事不曲從。

translations.literal: Congzhe could not rescue and correct this, yet only toward Prince Fu there was nothing he did not bend to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe could not remedy this, yet toward Prince Fu he bent to every demand.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗嘆皇上有為堯、舜之資，而輔佐無人。

translations.literal: Your servant once sighed that the emperor has the endowment to act as Yao or Shun, yet has no one to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once sighed that Your Majesty has the makings of a Yao or Shun, yet lacks worthy assistants.

sentences.zh: 僅得王家屏、沈鯉，又俱不信用。

translations.literal: He barely obtained Wang Jiaping and Shen Li, yet both alike were not employed in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiaping and Shen Li were barely secured, yet both were distrusted.

sentences.zh: 其余大抵庸惡陋劣，奸回冒嫉之徒，不意至從哲而風益下。

translations.literal: The rest are mostly mediocre, wicked, and base, treacherous, brazen, and jealous men—you would not expect that as far as Congzhe the wind grows still lower.
translations.idiomatic: The rest are mostly mediocre villains and treacherous, jealous men—you would not expect the moral climate to sink still lower with Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 臣聞從哲每向人言，輒雲內相之意，是甘為萬安、焦芳，曾趙誌臯，沈一貫之不若也。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard Congzhe whenever he speaks to others always says "the inner minister's intent"—this is willingly acting as Wan An and Jiao Fang once did, and is not even the equal of Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hears that Congzhe always says "the inner minister's intent" when he speaks to others—willingly playing Wan An and Jiao Fang, and not even equal to Zhao Zhigao and Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 從哲疏辨乞去。

translations.literal: Congzhe memorialized in defense begging to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe memorialized in defense begging to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留，而責春妄言瀆奏，出為福建右參議。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and retained him, but rebuked Chun for reckless words and disrespectful memorializing, sending him out as Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted and retained him, but rebuked Chun for reckless and disrespectful memorializing and sent him out as Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父艱。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起故官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 召為尚寶少卿，歷遷光祿卿。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals, he was promoted in due course to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Seals and promoted in due course to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏忠賢黨門克新劾春倚恃東林，父作子述，削籍歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wei Zhongxian's faction member Men Kexin impeached Chun for relying on the Donglin, the father composing and the son transmitting, and he was struck from the rolls and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Wei Zhongxian's follower Men Kexin impeached Chun for relying on the Donglin faction—"the father wrote and the son retailed it"—and he was struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年，召拜通政使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chongzhen, he was summoned and appointed Commissioner of the Transmission Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 9 (1636), he was summoned and appointed Commissioner of the Transmission Office.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部右侍郎，歷尚書。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, he rose in due course to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and in due course to Minister.

sentences.zh: 總督倉場，條行厘弊十事。

translations.literal: Superintending the granary depots, he drew up and implemented ten items to correct abuses.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the granary depots, he drew up and implemented ten reforms to correct abuses.

sentences.zh: 以勞瘁予告。

translations.literal: Because of exhaustion from labor he requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because of exhaustion from overwork he requested leave.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long, he was raised as Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was appointed Nanjing Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 疏請皇太子出閣，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the crown prince leave the palace study; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the crown prince leave the Eastern Palace for formal instruction; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 累疏引疾，不允。

translations.literal: Repeatedly memorializing on grounds of illness, he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized citing illness but was not permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 九年，條上戰守之策，並論賊三可擊狀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he itemized and submitted strategies for war and defense, and together discussed three conditions under which the bandits could be struck.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he submitted detailed strategies for offense and defense, and discussed three circumstances in which the rebels could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 帝如議敕行。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the discussion and ordered it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 十一年，黃道周、劉同升等諫楊嗣昌奪情，被貶謫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Huang Daozhou, Liu Tongsheng, and others remonstrated against Yang Sichang's recall from mourning, and were demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Huang Daozhou, Liu Tongsheng, and others remonstrated against Yang Sichang's recall from mourning and were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 範景文等疏救，春名與焉。

translations.literal: Fan Jingwen and others memorialized to rescue them; Chun's name was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jingwen and others memorialized in their defense; Chun's name was among the signatories.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，削景文籍，置春不問。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Jingwen was struck from the rolls; Chun was left unmentioned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Jingwen was struck from the rolls; Chun was left unpunished.

sentences.zh: 春為御史，甚有聲。

translations.literal: As investigating censor Chun had great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As investigating censor Chun had won great renown.

sentences.zh: 及居大僚，循職無咎。

translations.literal: When he reached high office, he followed his duties without fault.
translations.idiomatic: In high office he performed his duties without reproach.

sentences.zh: 會上疏請改折白糧，忤旨，罷歸。

translations.literal: On occasion he memorialized asking to change the conversion of white-grain tax, offended the edict, and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When he memorialized to reform the conversion of tribute grain tax, he offended the throne and was dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 是年卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 於孔兼，字元時，金壇人。

translations.literal: Yu Kongjian, styled Yuanshi, a man of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kongjian, styled Yuanshi, was a native of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 8 (1580).

sentences.zh: 授九江推官。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating magistrate of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部主事，再遷儀制郎中。

translations.literal: Entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and was promoted in two steps to director in the Bureau of Ritual Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and was twice promoted to director in the Bureau of Ritual Protocol.

sentences.zh: 疏論都御史吳時來晚節不終，不當謚忠恪，因請謚楊爵、陳瓚、孟秋。

translations.literal: He memorialized arguing that Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai's late years did not end well and he ought not receive the posthumous name Zhongke, and by the way asked posthumous names for Yang Jue, Chen Zan, and Meng Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai's late conduct did not merit the posthumous name Loyal and Reverent, and asked posthumous honors for Yang Jue, Chen Zan, and Meng Qiu.

sentences.zh: 乃奪時來謚，而謚爵忠介。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shilai's posthumous name was taken away, while Jue was given the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Shilai's posthumous name was thereupon revoked, while Jue was granted the name Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 大學士王家屏以爭冊立求去。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping because of contending over investiture as heir begged to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping resigned after contending over the heir's investiture.

sentences.zh: 孔兼上言：「陛下徇內嬖之情，而搖主鬯之器。

translations.literal: Kongjian submitted saying: "Your Majesty indulges the feelings of inner favorites, yet shakes the vessel of the state's chief sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Kongjian memorialized: "Your Majesty indulges inner favorites, yet shakes the vessel of the state's succession.

sentences.zh: 不納輔臣之言，反重諫官之罰。

translations.literal: You do not accept the chief ministers' words, yet on the contrary increase punishments on remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: You reject your chief ministers' counsel yet heap punishment on remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 且移怒吏部，削籍三人。

translations.literal: Moreover you shift anger to the Ministry of Personnel and strike three men from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: You have moreover vented your anger on the Ministry of Personnel, striking three men from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 夫萬國欽獲罪申時行，饒伸獲罪王錫爵，非獲罪於陛下也。

translations.literal: Now Wan Guoqin was punished because of Shen Shixing, Rao Shen because of Wang Xijue—they were not punished because of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Guoqin was punished because of Shen Shixing, Rao Shen because of Wang Xijue—they were not punished by Your Majesty's own decree.

sentences.zh: 輔臣於數千里外，能遙制朝權若此，毋乃陛下以此示恩，欲其復來共成他圖耶！

translations.literal: Chief ministers from several thousand li away can remotely control court power like this—might it not be that Your Majesty shows favor thus, wishing them to return and together accomplish another design!
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers thousands of li away can thus control the court from afar—does Your Majesty show them favor so they will return to pursue some other design together!

sentences.zh: 自陛下有近日之舉，而善類寒心，邪臣鼓掌。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty had the recent acts, good men are heartsick while wicked ministers clap their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's recent actions, good officials are disheartened while wicked ministers applaud.

sentences.zh: 將來逢君必巧，豫教無期，申生、楊廣再見於今，此宗廟之不利，非直臣等憂也。」

translations.literal: In future those who meet the ruler will surely be crafty, instruction without limit in advance—Shensheng and Yang Guang will appear again in our day; this is disadvantageous to the ancestral temple, not merely remonstrating ministers' worry.
translations.idiomatic: In future courtiers will grow ever craftier, tutors appointed without end—Shensheng and Yang Guang will appear again in our age; this harms the ancestral temple, not merely us remonstrating ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝得疏，怒甚。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial, he was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the memorial, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 已，竟留中。

translations.literal: In the end it was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，有詔並封三王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, there was an edict enfeoffing all three princes at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, an edict enfeoffed all three princes at once.

sentences.zh: 孔兼與員外郎陳泰來合疏爭曰：「立嫡之訓，自古有之。

translations.literal: Kong Jian and Vice Director Chen Tailai jointly submitted a memorial protesting, saying: "The teaching to establish the legitimate heir has existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jian and Vice Director Chen Tailai jointly memorialized in protest: "The rule that the legitimate heir must be established is as old as the state itself.

sentences.zh: 然歷考祖宗以來，未有虛東宮之位以候嫡子者。

translations.literal: Yet examining all generations since the founding ancestors, there has never been one who left the Eastern Palace vacant to await a son of the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in all the generations since the founding of the dynasty, no ruler has ever left the Eastern Palace empty while waiting for a son of the principal consort.

sentences.zh: 昔陛下正位東宮，年甫六歲，仁聖皇太后方在盛年，先皇帝曾不少待，陛下豈不省記乎？

translations.literal: Formerly when Your Majesty was installed in the Eastern Palace, you were only six years old; the Benevolent and Sagely Empress Dowager was still in her prime, and the late emperor did not hesitate in the least—does Your Majesty not recall?
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was made heir, you were only six; the Benevolent and Sagely Empress Dowager was still young, and the late emperor did not delay a day—surely Your Majesty remembers?

sentences.zh: 地逼則嫌生，禮殊則分定。

translations.literal: When positions press close, suspicion arises; when rites differ, divisions are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When heirs stand too close together, suspicion is born; when ritual distinctions are clear, ranks are settled.

sentences.zh: 願收還新諭，建儲、封王一時並舉，宗社幸甚。」

translations.literal: I pray you withdraw the recent edict and establish the heir and enfeoff princes in one act—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: We pray that Your Majesty withdraw the recent edict and establish the heir and enfeoff the princes in a single act—the realm would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply was issued.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 孔兼又言：「陛下堅持待嫡之說，既疑群臣謗訕，又謂朝綱倒持，遂欲坐諫者以無禮於君之罪。

translations.literal: Kong Jian also said: "Your Majesty stubbornly holds to waiting for the son of the principal wife, both suspecting that ministers slander you and declaring that court norms are inverted, and thus wish to punish remonstrators with the crime of disrespect toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jian added: "Your Majesty clings to waiting for a son of the principal consort, suspecting ministers of slandering you and claiming that court norms have been turned upside down—and now you would punish remonstrators with the crime of disrespect to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夫謂元子當立不容緩者，君子也。

translations.literal: Those who say the eldest son ought to be established without delay are gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say the eldest son must be established without delay are gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 此有禮於君者，王如堅諸人是也。

translations.literal: These show respect toward the ruler—men such as Wang Rujian.
translations.idiomatic: These are men who show respect to their ruler—Wang Rujian and his like.

sentences.zh: 謂並封可行逢上意者，小人也。

translations.literal: Those who say simultaneous enfeoffment is feasible because it suits the emperor's wish are petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say simultaneous enfeoffment is acceptable because it flatters the throne are petty men.

sentences.zh: 此無禮於君者，許夢熊一人是也。

translations.literal: These show disrespect toward the ruler—Xu Mengxiong alone.
translations.idiomatic: These are men who show disrespect to their ruler—Xu Mengxiong alone.

sentences.zh: 今欲以無禮之罪，而加之有禮於其君者，何以服人心，昭國法？

translations.literal: Now to impose the crime of disrespect on those who show respect to their ruler—how will this win hearts or clarify the laws of the state?
translations.idiomatic: To punish men of respect with the crime of disrespect—how will that win hearts or vindicate the law of the land?

sentences.zh: 臣又惟巫蠱之謗啟於堯母；

translations.literal: Your servant further considers that slander of witchcraft began with the mother of Yao;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further reflects that charges of witchcraft first arose from a mother's jealousy;

sentences.zh: 承乾之誅成於偏愛。

translations.literal: the execution of Chengqian was brought about by partial favor.
translations.idiomatic: and the destruction of Li Chengqian was wrought by a father's partial love.

sentences.zh: 自古亂臣，未有不窺人君之隙而逢迎以遂其奸者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity no rebellious minister has failed to watch for openings in his ruler's conduct and flatter him to achieve his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious ministers in every age have watched for cracks in their ruler's judgment and flattered him to advance their treachery.

sentences.zh: 始錫爵之兩諭並擬，其負國誤君大矣。

translations.literal: At the outset Xijue's two edicts were both drafted together—his offense against the state and misleadership of the ruler is very great.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Wang Xijue drafted both edicts together—his offense against the state and betrayal of the ruler is grave indeed.

sentences.zh: 既不能轉移君心決計於初，乃以杜門求去為計。

translations.literal: Unable to turn the ruler's heart and fix his resolve at the beginning, he took closing his gates and seeking to leave as his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to turn the emperor's heart at the first, he made his strategy one of shutting his gates and threatening resignation.

sentences.zh: 夫前無失策，一去可以成名。

translations.literal: When there had been no mistaken policy before, one departure could have made a name.
translations.idiomatic: Had he never erred, a single resignation might have won him lasting honor.

sentences.zh: 失而後爭，爭而不得，雖去不足塞責矣。

translations.literal: Struggling only after a loss, and when struggle avails nothing—even departure is not enough to discharge responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: To struggle only after defeat, and when struggle fails—even resignation cannot absolve him.

sentences.zh: 人謂錫爵言無不盡，特苦陛下聽斷之不行。

translations.literal: Men say Xijue left nothing unsaid, and only regretted that Your Majesty would not heed his judgments.
translations.idiomatic: Men say Wang Xijue left nothing unsaid and blamed only Your Majesty's refusal to heed him.

sentences.zh: 臣則雲陛下悔心已萌，特憂錫爵感孚之未至。

translations.literal: Your servant says the emperor's regret has already sprouted, yet he worries Xijue's persuasive touch has not yet reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes regret has already stirred in Your Majesty's breast, and that you fear only that Wang Xijue has not yet felt it.

sentences.zh: 若姑雲徐徐，坐視君父之過舉，錫爵縱不為宗社計，獨不為身名計乎？」

translations.literal: If you merely say "gradually," sitting by while ruler and father err—is Xijue not concerned even for his reputation, if not for the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: If you merely counsel delay while your lord and father blunder—will Wang Xijue spare no thought even for his own name, if not for the altars of the realm?

sentences.zh: 會廷臣多諫者，其事竟寢。

translations.literal: As many court officials joined in memorializing, the matter was abandoned in the end.
translations.idiomatic: As court officials memorialized in growing numbers, the affair was abandoned in the end.

sentences.zh: 亡何，考功郎中趙南星坐京察削籍。

translations.literal: Before long, Director Zhao Nanxing was stripped from the rolls for an offense in the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Director Zhao Nanxing was struck from the rolls in the capital personnel evaluation.

sentences.zh: 孔兼、泰來各疏救。

translations.literal: Kong Jian and Tailai each submitted memorials in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jian and Chen Tailai each submitted memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝積前恨，謫孔兼安吉判官，泰來饒平典史。

translations.literal: The emperor, nursing old resentments, demoted Kong Jian to Assistant Magistrate of Anji and Tailai to Record Keeper of Raoping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, nursing old resentments, demoted Kong Jian to assistant magistrate of Anji and Chen Tailai to record keeper of Raoping.

sentences.zh: 孔兼投牒歸。

translations.literal: Kong Jian submitted his credentials and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jian handed in his credentials and went home.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，杜門讀書，矩矱整肅，鄉人稱之無間言。

translations.literal: He lived at home twenty years, reading behind closed doors, his conduct severely disciplined—fellow townspeople praised him without a dissenting word.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement twenty years, reading behind closed doors with stern discipline; neighbors praised him without a whisper of reproach.

sentences.zh: 泰來，字伯符，平湖人。

translations.literal: Tailai, styled Bofu, was a native of Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tailai, styled Bofu, was a native of Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 年十九，舉萬歷五年進士，授順天教授，進國子博士。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli, was appointed Professor of Shuntian, and advanced to Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the jinshi in Wanli 5, was appointed professor of Shuntian, and advanced to erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 見執政與言路相水火，上書規之，坐是五年不調。

translations.literal: Seeing the chief ministers and the remonstrating offices locked in conflict, he submitted a memorial admonishing them and for this went five years without transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chief ministers and remonstrating offices locked in bitter conflict, he memorialized to admonish them and for this went five years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 南京禮部郎中馬應圖，泰來同邑，又同年生也，十三年，上疏譏切執政，又力詆給事中齊世臣，御史龔懋賢、蔡系周、孫愈賢、吳定，而盛稱吳中行、趙用賢、沈思孝、李植諸人。

translations.literal: Ma Yingtu, Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, was from the same district and the same year of birth; in the thirteenth year he submitted a memorial sharply criticizing the chief ministers and strenuously denounced the supervising secretaries Qi Shichen and the censors Gong Maoxian, Cai Xizhou, Sun Yuxian, and Wu Ding, while warmly praising Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Shen Sixiao, and Li Zhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yingtu, a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, was from the same district and the same examination year; in Wanli 13 he submitted a memorial sharply rebuking the chief ministers and fiercely denounced supervising secretaries Qi Shichen and censors Gong Maoxian, Cai Xizhou, Sun Yuxian, and Wu Ding, while warmly praising Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Shen Sixiao, Li Zhi, and others.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，謫大同典史。

translations.literal: Disobeying the imperial will, he was demoted to Record Keeper of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Disobeying the throne, he was demoted to record keeper of Datong.

sentences.zh: 給事中王致祥、御史柴祥等希執政意，復連章劾應圖，且言泰來為點定奏章。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Zhixiang, Censor Chai Xiang, and others currying favor with the chief ministers again submitted consecutive memorials impeaching Yingtu, and moreover said Tailai had revised the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Zhixiang, Censor Chai Xiang, and others currying favor with the chief ministers again impeached Yingtu in successive memorials, and claimed that Chen Tailai had polished the draft.

sentences.zh: 帝以應圖既貶不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, since Yingtu was already demoted, did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yingtu was already punished, the emperor did not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 泰來引疾歸。

translations.literal: Tailai cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tailai cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起禮部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 疏請建儲，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting establishment of the heir—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting that the heir be established; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 逾年遂卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: The following year he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，孔兼、泰來俱贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi era, Kong Jian and Tailai were both posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign, Kong Jian and Chen Tailai were both posthumously granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 於氏為金壇望族。

translations.literal: The Yu clan was a prominent family of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu clan was a leading family of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 孔兼祖湛，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Kong Jian's grandfather Zhan was Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Jian's grandfather Zhan had been vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 兄文熙，大名兵備副使。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wenkai was Vice Commissioner for Military Preparedness at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wenkai was vice commissioner for military preparedness at Daming.

sentences.zh: 再從弟仕廉，南京戶部侍郎，有清望。

translations.literal: His second cousin once removed Shilian was Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, with a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His second cousin once removed Shilian was vice minister of revenue at Nanjing, famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 史孟麟，字際明，宜興人。

translations.literal: Shi Menglin, styled Jiming, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Menglin, styled Jiming, was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Wanli 11.

sentences.zh: 授庶吉士，改吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Compiler, then transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed junior compiler, then transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏劾少詹事黃洪憲典試作奸，左都御史吳時來沮抑言路。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Junior Tutor Huang Hongxian for misconduct in presiding over examinations, and Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai for suppressing the remonstrating offices.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized impeaching Junior Tutor Huang Hongxian for corruption in the examinations and Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai for throttling the remonstrating offices.

sentences.zh: 執政庇之，格不行。

translations.literal: The chief ministers shielded them and blocked implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers shielded them and blocked the memorial.

sentences.zh: 員外郎趙南星、主事姜士昌相繼劾兩人，並及副都御史詹仰庇。

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhao Nanxing and Chief Clerk Jiang Shichang successively impeached the two men, extending also to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhao Nanxing and Chief Clerk Jiang Shichang successively impeached the two men and extended their charges to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi.

sentences.zh: 執政滋不說。

translations.literal: The chief ministers grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers grew ever more displeased.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中陳與郊素附執政，屬同官李春開三疏訐南星、士昌妄言。

translations.literal: Chen Yuhe, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, had long sided with the chief ministers and directed his colleague Li Chunkai to submit three memorials accusing Nanxing and Shichang of reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuhe, chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel, had long sided with the chief ministers and urged his colleague Li Chunkai to submit three memorials accusing Nanxing and Shichang of reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 帝止下春開疏，而留南星、士昌奏不發。

translations.literal: The emperor only sent down Chunkai's memorial, while holding back Nanxing and Shichang's submissions without issuing them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued only Chunkai's memorial, withholding Nanxing's and Shichang's submissions.

sentences.zh: 給事中王繼光、萬自約不平，復抗章論時來等，詞甚峻切。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wang Jiguang and Wan Ziyue, resenting the injustice, again submitted defiant memorials discussing Shilai and others, their language very stern.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Wang Jiguang and Wan Ziyue, indignant at the injustice, again memorialized against Shilai and others in language fiercely stern.

sentences.zh: 孟麟亦上疏力攻春開，語並侵執政，因求罷，不許。

translations.literal: Menglin also submitted a memorial forcefully attacking Chunkai, language extending to the chief ministers as well; he then begged dismissal—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Menglin also memorialized, attacking Chunkai with force and implicating the chief ministers; he then begged to be dismissed, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 孟麟竟自引歸。

translations.literal: Menglin ultimately resigned on his own initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Menglin ultimately resigned on his own.

sentences.zh: 春開亦謝病去，後以考察罷。

translations.literal: Chunkai also begged leave for illness and left; later he was dismissed in the personnel evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Chunkai also begged leave on grounds of illness; later he was dismissed in the personnel evaluation.

sentences.zh: 孟麟尋召為兵科右給事中。

translations.literal: Menglin was soon recalled as Right Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Menglin was soon recalled as right supervising secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二十年，大學士趙誌臯、張位言：「凡會議會推，並令廷臣類奏，取自上裁，用杜專權。」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei said: "For all joint deliberations and joint recommendations, let court officials submit classified memorials for the emperor's decision, to cut off monopoly of power.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 20, Grand Secretaries Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei proposed: "For all joint deliberations and joint recommendations, let court officials submit classified memorials for the emperor's decision, to forestall monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 孟麟疏爭曰：「自臣通籍以來，竊見閣臣侵部院之權，言路希閣臣之指，官失其守，言失其責久矣。

translations.literal: Menglin memorialized in protest: "Since I entered the register, I have privately observed ministers of the Secretariat encroaching on the powers of the ministries and commissions, and the remonstrating offices currying Secretariat favor—officials have lost their stations and remonstrators their charge for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Menglin memorialized in protest: "Since I entered office I have watched Secretariat ministers encroach on the ministries and remonstrating offices curry Secretariat favor—officials have lost their posts and remonstrators their charge for years.

sentences.zh: 陛下更置輔臣，與天下更始，政事歸六部，公論付言官，天下方欣欣望治，奈何忽有此令？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly appointed chief ministers for a fresh start with the realm; government affairs should return to the Six Ministries and public opinion to remonstrating officials—all under heaven were looking hopefully toward good governance; how can you suddenly issue such an order?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly appointed chief ministers for a fresh beginning; affairs of state were to return to the Six Ministries and public opinion to remonstrating officials—all the realm looked toward good government; how can you suddenly issue such an order?

sentences.zh: 曩太祖罷中書省，分設六部，恐其專也；

translations.literal: Formerly the founding emperor abolished the Secretariat and established the Six Ministries separately, fearing their monopoly;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the founding emperor abolished the Secretariat and divided the Six Ministries, fearing monopoly;

sentences.zh: 而官各有職，不相侵越，則又惟恐其不專。

translations.literal: yet when each officer had his duty and none encroached on another, he also feared only that they would not hold monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: yet when each officer held his charge and none trespassed on another, he also feared only that they would not be fully responsible.

sentences.zh: 蓋以一事任一官，則專不為害；

translations.literal: For when one matter is entrusted to one officer, monopoly does no harm;
translations.idiomatic: When one matter is entrusted to one officer, concentration does no harm;

sentences.zh: 即使敗事，亦罪有所歸。

translations.literal: even if affairs go wrong, guilt has somewhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: and if affairs go wrong, blame has somewhere to fall.

sentences.zh: 此祖宗建官之意也。

translations.literal: This was the founding emperor's intent in establishing offices.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the founding emperor's intent in establishing offices.

sentences.zh: 今令諸臣各書所見，類奏以聽上裁，則始以一部之事，分而散之於諸司；

translations.literal: Now ordering all officials to write their views and submit them classified for the sovereign's decision—at first a matter of one ministry is divided and scattered among the various bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: Now to order all officials to write their views and submit them classified for imperial decision—at first a matter of one ministry is split and scattered among the bureaus;

sentences.zh: 究以諸司之權，合而收之於禁密。

translations.literal: in the end the powers of the various bureaus are gathered and drawn back into the forbidden inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: in the end the powers of the bureaus are gathered back into the forbidden inner court.

sentences.zh: 事雖上裁，旨由閣擬。

translations.literal: Though matters are decided by the throne, the rescripts come from Secretariat drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Though matters are decided by the throne, the rescripts are drafted in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 脫有私意奸其間，內托上旨，外諉廷言，誰執其咎？

translations.literal: If private aims insert malice between them, using the inner to entrust it to the imperial will and the outer to shift blame to court opinion—who will bear the guilt?
translations.idiomatic: If private designs slip between them, invoking the imperial will within and shifting blame to the court without—who will bear the guilt?

sentences.zh: 又脫有馮保、張居正者，夤緣為奸，授意外廷，小人趨承，扶同罔上，朝廷不得察其非，當官不能爭其是，又誰執其咎？

translations.literal: Again if there should be another Feng Bao or Zhang Juzheng, who by clinging connections do evil and give unexpected orders to the outer court while petty men rush to comply and jointly deceive the throne—so that the court cannot perceive what is wrong and incumbent officials cannot dispute what is right—who then will bear the guilt?
translations.idiomatic: And if another Feng Bao or Zhang Juzheng should rise, who by patronage do evil and issue unexpected orders to the outer court while petty men rush to obey and jointly deceive the throne—so that the court cannot see what is wrong and officials cannot dispute what is right—who then will bear the guilt?

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂政權分之六部，不可以為專。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that governmental power divided among the Six Ministries must not be made monopolized.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that power divided among the Six Ministries must not be allowed to become monopoly.

sentences.zh: 惟六部不專，則必有專之者。

translations.literal: Only when the Six Ministries are not monopolized will there necessarily be someone who monopolizes them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Ministries are not allowed their charge, someone else will necessarily monopolize power.

sentences.zh: 是乃收攬威權之漸，必不可從也。」

translations.literal: This is the first step toward gathering authoritarian power in one hand—it absolutely must not be followed."
translations.idiomatic: This is the first step toward concentrating power in one hand—it must not be followed."

sentences.zh: 忤旨，不納。

translations.literal: Disobeying the imperial will, it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Disobeying the throne, the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 三王並封議起，孟麟、於孔兼等詣王錫爵邸爭之。

translations.literal: When the controversy over enfeoffing the three princes together arose, Menglin, Kong Jian, and others went to Wang Xijue's residence to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: When the controversy over enfeoffing the three princes together arose, Menglin, Kong Jian, and others went to Wang Xijue's residence to argue with him.

sentences.zh: 又進《或問》一篇，別白尤力。

translations.literal: He also advanced a "Questions and Answers" piece, distinguishing the issues with special force.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a piece entitled "Questions and Answers," clarifying the issues with exceptional force.

sentences.zh: 尚書孫鑨、考功郎中趙南星掌癸巳京察，孟麟實佐之。

translations.literal: Minister Sun Sai and Director Zhao Nanxing presided over the guisi capital evaluation, with Menglin assisting in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Sun Sai and Director Zhao Nanxing presided over the guisi capital evaluation, with Menglin assisting in practice.

sentences.zh: 南星以讒言斥，孟麟亦引疾歸。

translations.literal: Nanxing was expelled on slanderous charges, and Menglin also cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Nanxing was expelled on slanderous charges, and Menglin also cited illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 召拜太仆少卿，復以疾去。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, but again left on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, but again left on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 孟麟素砥名節，復與東林講會，時望益重。

translations.literal: Menglin had always polished his moral reputation and again joined the Donglin lecture gatherings—his standing in the age grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: Menglin had always burnished his moral reputation and again joined the Donglin lecture gatherings; his standing in the age grew ever weightier.

sentences.zh: 家居十五年，召起故官，督四夷館。

translations.literal: After fifteen years at home he was recalled to his former post and supervised the Four Barbarian Offices.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years in retirement he was recalled to his former post and supervised the Four Barbarian Offices.

sentences.zh: 會睹梃擊事，疏請冊立皇太孫，絕群小覬覦之望。

translations.literal: When the stick-assault affair occurred, he memorialized requesting investiture of the imperial great-grandson to cut off petty men's hopes of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: When the stick-assault affair broke, he memorialized requesting investiture of the imperial great-grandson to cut off petty men's hopes of usurpation.

sentences.zh: 且救御史劉光復。

translations.literal: He also interceded for Censor Liu Guangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He also interceded for Censor Liu Guangfu.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫兩浙鹽運判官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and demoted him to Salt Transport Assistant of the two Zhe provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to salt transport assistant of the two Zhe provinces.

sentences.zh: 熹宗立，稍遷南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: When Xizong ascended, he was gradually transferred to Chief Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianqi Emperor ascended, he was gradually transferred to chief clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 累擢太仆卿，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and died in office.

sentences.zh: 薛敷教，字以身，武進人。

translations.literal: Xue Fujiao, styled Yishen, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fujiao, styled Yishen, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 祖應旗，字仲常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingqi, styled Zhongchang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingqi, styled Zhongchang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the fourteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiajing 14.

sentences.zh: 由慈溪知縣屢遷南京考功郎中，主京察。

translations.literal: From Magistrate of Cixi he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, presiding over the capital evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Cixi he rose repeatedly to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, presiding over the capital evaluation.

sentences.zh: 大學士嚴嵩嘗為給事中王曄所劾，囑尚寶丞諸傑貽書應旗，令黜曄。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yan Song had once been impeached by Supervising Secretary Wang Ye; he instructed Senior Court Gentleman Zhu Jie to send Yingqi a letter asking him to demote Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Song had once been impeached by Supervising Secretary Wang Ye; he instructed Senior Court Gentleman Zhu Jie to write Yingqi asking him to demote Ye.

sentences.zh: 應旗反黜傑，嵩大怒。

translations.literal: Yingqi instead demoted Jie, and Song was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi instead demoted Jie, and Yan Song was furious.

sentences.zh: 應旗又黜常州知府符驗，嵩令御史桂榮劾應旗挾私黜郡守，謫建昌通判。

translations.literal: Yingqi also demoted Prefect of Changzhou Fu Yan; Song had Censor Gui Rong impeach Yingqi for using personal grudges to demote a prefect, and he was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi also demoted Changzhou prefect Fu Yan; Yan Song had Censor Gui Rong impeach Yingqi for demoting a prefect out of private spite, and he was demoted to assistant prefect of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 歷浙江提學副使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Vice Commissioner of Education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice commissioner of education in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 應旗雅工場屋文字，與王鏊、唐順之、瞿景淳齊名。

translations.literal: Yingqi was accomplished in examination-hall prose and ranked with Wang Ao, Tang Shunzhi, and Qu Jingchun in fame.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi excelled in examination-hall prose and ranked in fame with Wang Ao, Tang Shunzhi, and Qu Jingchun.

sentences.zh: 其閱文所品題，百不失一。

translations.literal: In reading papers what he graded and annotated was correct ninety-nine times in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In grading examination papers his judgments were right ninety-nine times in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 以大計罷歸，顧憲成兄弟方少，從之學，敷教遂與善，用風節相期許。

translations.literal: Dismissed and returned home in the grand evaluation, when the Gu Xiancheng brothers were still young they studied with him; Fujiao thus befriended them and pledged integrity of character to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed in the grand evaluation and returned home, he took the Gu Xiancheng brothers as pupils while they were still young; Fujiao befriended them and they pledged one another to lives of integrity.

sentences.zh: 及舉萬歷十七年進士，與高攀龍同出趙南星門，益以名教自任。

translations.literal: When he passed the jinshi in the seventeenth year of Wanli, he and Gao Panlong came from Zhao Nanxing's school together and took all the more upon themselves the charge of moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed the jinshi in Wanli 17, he and Gao Panlong were both pupils of Zhao Nanxing and took all the more upon themselves the charge of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 會南京御史王藩臣疏劾巡撫周繼，不具揭都察院，為其長耿定向所劾。

translations.literal: When Nanjing Censor Wang Fanchen memorialized impeaching Grand Coordinator Zhou Ji, he did not submit a report to the Censorate; his chief Geng Dingxiang impeached him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing Censor Wang Fanchen impeached Grand Coordinator Zhou Ji without filing a report with the Censorate, his superior Geng Dingxiang impeached him in turn.

sentences.zh: 左都御史吳時來因請申飭憲規，藩臣坐停俸。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai therefore asked to enforce the censorial regulations; Fanchen was punished by suspension of salary.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai requested stricter enforcement of censorial rules, and Fanchen's salary was suspended.

sentences.zh: 敷教上言：「時來壅遏言路，代人狼噬。

translations.literal: Fujiao memorialized: "Shilai obstructs the remonstrating path, and on others' behalf does the wolf's tearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fujiao memorialized: "Shilai chokes off frank remonstrance and lets others devour their victims like wolves.

sentences.zh: 而二三輔臣，曲學險诐，又故繩庶寀，以崇九列，塞主上聰明。

translations.literal: And the second and third chief ministers, their crooked learning treacherous and devious, again deliberately bind the many minor officials to elevate the nine ranks, blocking the sovereign's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the chief ministers pursue crooked, treacherous learning, binding minor officials to elevate the Nine Ranks and blind Your Majesty's discernment.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴黨邪之禁，更易兩都臺長，以清風憲。」

translations.literal: One ought strictly to forbid factional wickedness, replace the heads of both capitals' censorates, to clear the wind of law.
translations.idiomatic: Strictly forbid factional wickedness and replace the heads of both capitals' censorates to restore integrity to the law.

sentences.zh: 疏上，大學士申時行等疏言：「故事，御史建白，北京即日投揭臺長，南京則以三日。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Grand Secretaries Shen Shixing and others memorialized: "By precedent, when a censor puts forward a proposal, in Beijing he submits a report to the censorate chief the same day; at Nanjing within three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others replied: "By precedent a censor's proposal in Beijing is reported to the censorate chief that same day; at Nanjing within three days.

sentences.zh: 藩臣廢故事，薄罰未為過。

translations.literal: Fanchen abandoned precedent; a light punishment is not excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Fanchen broke precedent; a light penalty was not excessive.

sentences.zh: 必如敷教言，將盡抑大臣而後可耶？」

translations.literal: Must it be as Fujiao says, suppressing all grand ministers before it can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Must we, as Fujiao demands, suppress every grand minister before this is settled?

sentences.zh: 副都御史詹仰庇劾敷教煽惑人心，淆亂國是。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi impeached Fujiao for stirring people's hearts and confusing what is right for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yangbi impeached Fujiao for stirring public emotion and confusing state policy.

sentences.zh: 詔敷教歸，省過三年，以教職用。

translations.literal: Ordered Fujiao to return home, reflect on faults three years, then use in teaching office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fujiao home to reflect for three years before appointment to a teaching post.

sentences.zh: 大學士許國以敷教其門生，而疏語侵己，尤憤，自請罷斥。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Guo, because Fujiao was his student yet the memorial's language encroached on himself, was especially angry and asked to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Guo, whose student Fujiao had been, was especially furious at the memorial's attack on him and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 因言：「邇來建言成風，可要名，可躐秩，又可掩過，故人競趨之為捷徑，此風既成，莫可救止。

translations.literal: Saying: "Recently remonstrance has become a fashion—one may seek a name, leap ranks, or cover faults; therefore men vie for this shortcut; once this wind is established it cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Remonstrance has lately become a fashion—for reputation, promotion, or covering faults. Men rush this shortcut; once entrenched, it cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 方今京師訛言東南赤旱，臣未為憂，而獨憂此區區者，彼止一時之災，此則世道之慮也。」

translations.literal: Now in the capital rumors say drought in the southeast; your servant is not worried about that, only about this petty matter—for that is a temporary disaster, this a worry for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors speak of drought in the southeast; I do not fear that disaster but this trend—for drought passes; this corrupts the age.

sentences.zh: 時來亦乞休，力詆敷教及主事饒伸。

translations.literal: Shixing also begged to retire, forcefully denouncing Fujiao and Secretary Rao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing also begged retirement, fiercely denouncing Fujiao and Secretary Rao Shen.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留國、時來。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and retained Gu and Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted them and kept Gu and Shixing in office.

sentences.zh: 都給事中陳與郊復上疏極詆建言諸臣，帝亦不問。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao again memorialized extremely denouncing remonstrating officials; the emperor also did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Chen Yujiao memorialized again, savagely denouncing remonstrators; the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏，起敷教鳳翔教授，旋遷國子助教。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year, Fujiao was raised as professor of Fengxiang, soon transferred to assistant instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the twentieth year Fujiao was appointed professor at Fengxiang, soon promoted to assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 明年，力爭三王並封，又上書王錫爵。

translations.literal: The next year, he forcefully contended the simultaneous enfeoffment of three princes, and again wrote to Wang Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he fiercely opposed enfeoffing three princes at once and wrote again to Wang Xijue.

sentences.zh: 尋以救南星，謫光州學正。

translations.literal: Before long, for rescuing Nanxing, he was banished to instructor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For defending Nanxing he was soon banished to instructor at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 省母歸，遂不復出。

translations.literal: Visiting his mother in mourning and returning home, he never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 敷教禔身嚴苦，垢衣糲食，終身未嘗受人饋。

translations.literal: Fujiao disciplined his person with stern austerity, worn clothes and coarse food; his whole life he never accepted gifts from others.
translations.idiomatic: Fujiao lived with harsh austerity—tattered clothes, plain food—and never accepted gifts.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，力持清議，大吏有舉動，多用敷教言而止。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home twenty years, he vigorously upheld pure criticism; when great officials took action, they often stopped because of Fujiao's words.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years at home he upheld principled criticism; great officials often abandoned plans on his word.

sentences.zh: 後與憲成兄弟及攀龍輩講學。

translations.literal: Later he lectured with the Gu brothers and Panlong's company.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lectured with the Gu brothers, Gao Panlong, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚寶司丞。

translations.literal: On death, posthumously granted Registrar of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously granted Registrar of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 安希範，字小範，無錫人。

translations.literal: An Xifan, styled Xiaofan, a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: An Xifan, styled Xiaofan, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the metropolitan examination in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 14 (1586).

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: Appointed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed court attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部主事，乞便養母，改南京吏部。

translations.literal: Promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites, begged convenient posting to nurture mother, transferred to Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites, he asked leave to care for his mother and was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，行人高攀龍以趙用賢去國，疏爭之，與鄭材、楊應宿相訐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, attendant Gao Panlong because Zhao Yongxian left the capital memorialized in protest, mutually denouncing Zheng Cai and Yang Yingsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Attendant Gao Panlong, after Zhao Yongxian left court, memorialized in protest and crossed words with Zheng Cai and Yang Yingsu.

sentences.zh: 攀龍謫揭陽典史。

translations.literal: Panlong was banished to recorder of Jieyang.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong was banished to recorder of Jieyang.

sentences.zh: 御史吳弘濟復爭，亦被黜。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Hongji again remonstrated and was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Hongji remonstrated again and was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 希範上疏曰：「近年以來，正直之臣不安於位。

translations.literal: Xifan memorialized: "In recent years upright officials cannot rest in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan memorialized: "In recent years upright officials cannot keep their posts.

sentences.zh: 趙南星、孟化鯉為選郎，秉公持正，乃次第屏黜。

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing and Meng Huaji as selection directors held public office with integrity, yet were dismissed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nanxing and Meng Huaji served as selection directors with integrity, yet were dismissed in turn.

sentences.zh: 趙用賢節概震天下，止以吳鎮豎子一疏而歸，使應宿、材得窺意指，交章攻擊。

translations.literal: Zhao Yongxian's integrity shook all under heaven; only because of one memorial by Wu Zhen, a shallow fellow, did he return—letting Yingsu and Cai spy out intent and link memorials to attack.
