translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yongxian's integrity was famed throughout the realm; one memorial from the shallow fellow Wu Zhen sent him home, letting Yingsu and Cai read the court's mood and attack in concert.

sentences.zh: 至如孫鑨之清修公正，李世達之練達剛明，李禎之孤介廉方，並朝廷儀表。

translations.literal: As for Sun Luan's pure uprightness and fairness, Li Shida's seasoned firmness and clarity, Li Zhen's solitary integrity and probity—all were the court's models.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Luan was pure and upright, Li Shida seasoned and firm, Li Zhen solitary and incorruptible—each a model for the court.

sentences.zh: 鑨、世達先後去國，禎亦堅懷去誌，天下共惜諸臣不用，而疑閣臣冒嫉，不使竟其用也。

translations.literal: Luan and Shida left the capital in succession; Zhen also firmly harbored intent to leave—all under heaven together lamented these officials unused, and suspected the chief ministers of jealous obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Luan and Shida left in succession; Zhen also meant to resign. The realm lamented such men unused and suspected the chief ministers of jealous obstruction.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍一疏，正直和平，此陛下忠臣，亦輔臣諍友。

translations.literal: Gao Panlong's one memorial was upright and peaceful—this is Your Majesty's loyal minister and also the chief ministers' remonstrating friend.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong's memorial was upright and measured—Your Majesty's loyal minister and the chief ministers' candid friend.

sentences.zh: 至如應宿辨疏，塗面喪心，無復人理。

translations.literal: As for Yingsu's rebuttal memorial—it besmeared his face and lost his heart, without humanity's reason left.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingsu's rebuttal smeared his own face and abandoned reason entirely.

sentences.zh: 明旨下部科勘議，未嘗不是攀龍非應宿。

translations.literal: The clear edict sent down to the ministries and offices for joint deliberation never failed to fault Panlong, not Yingsu.
translations.idiomatic: The edict sent to ministries for joint deliberation always faulted Panlong, not Yingsu.

sentences.zh: 及奉處分之詔，則應宿僅從薄謫，攀龍反竄炎荒。

translations.literal: Yet when the disposition edict came, Yingsu only received light demotion while Panlong was cast to the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when punishment was ordered, Yingsu was lightly demoted while Panlong was exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 輔臣誤國不忠，無甚於此。

translations.literal: Chief ministers' disloyalty to the state—nothing worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers' disloyalty to the state could hardly be worse.

sentences.zh: 乃動輒自文，諉之宸斷。

translations.literal: Yet they constantly gloss over themselves, attributing to the imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they constantly excuse themselves, attributing all to imperial decision alone.

sentences.zh: 坐視君父過舉，弼違補袞之謂何！

translations.literal: Sitting by while ruler and father err—what of assisting and correcting, mending the royal robe!
translations.idiomatic: They watch the ruler and father err—what of the minister's duty to assist and correct!

sentences.zh: 茍俟降斥之後，陽為申救，以愚天下耳目，而天下早已知其肺腑矣。

translations.literal: If only after demotion they falsely plead rescue to deceive all under heaven's eyes—yet all under heaven already know their insides.
translations.idiomatic: If after demotion they feign rescue to fool the realm, the realm already knows their hearts.

sentences.zh: 吳弘濟辨別君子小人，較若蒼素，乃與攀龍相繼得罪。

translations.literal: Wu Hongji's distinction of gentlemen and petty men was clearer than black and white; yet like Panlong he successively suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hongji distinguished gentleman from petty man as clearly as black from white; yet like Panlong he was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 臣之所惜，不為二臣，正恐君子皆退，小人皆進，誰為受其禍者。

translations.literal: What your servant laments is not the two officials—only fears that all gentlemen withdraw and petty men advance; who will bear the calamity?
translations.idiomatic: I do not lament for those two alone—I fear that when gentlemen withdraw and petty men advance, the calamity falls on all.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下立斥應宿、材，為小人媚竈之戒；

translations.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty immediately dismiss Yingsu and Cai as warning to petty men currying the kitchen hearth;
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty dismiss Yingsu and Cai at once as a warning to petty men who curry favor at the kitchen hearth;

sentences.zh: 復攀龍、弘濟官，以獎忠良；

translations.literal: restore Panlong and Hongji's offices to reward the loyal;
translations.idiomatic: restore Panlong and Hongji to reward loyal service;

sentences.zh: 並嚴諭閣臣王錫爵，無挾私植黨，仇視正人。

translations.literal: and sternly admonish chief minister Wang Xijue not to harbor private factions and hate upright men.
translations.idiomatic: and sternly warn Grand Secretary Wang Xijue against private factions and hatred of upright men.

sentences.zh: 則相業光而聖德亦光矣。」

translations.literal: Then the minister's achievement would shine and the sage's virtue also shine.
translations.idiomatic: Then the minister's service would shine—and so would Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 時南京刑部郎中譚一召、主事孫繼有方以劾錫爵被譴。

translations.literal: At that time Nanjing Ministry of Punishments Director Tan Yizhao and Secretary Sun Jiyou had been punished for impeaching Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Nanjing Punishments Director Tan Yizhao and Secretary Sun Jiyou had been punished for impeaching Xijue.

sentences.zh: 希範疏入，帝怒，斥為民。

translations.literal: When Xifan's memorial entered, the emperor was angry and dismissed him to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Xifan's memorial arrived, the emperor in anger dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 希範恬靜簡易，與東林講學之會。

translations.literal: Xifan was tranquil, simple, and easy; he joined the Donglin lecture meetings.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan was tranquil and unassuming and joined the Donglin assemblies.

sentences.zh: 熹宗嗣位，將起官，先卒。

translations.literal: When Xizong succeeded, he was about to be recalled to office but died first.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong succeeded, he was to be recalled but died first.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 吳弘濟，字春陽，秀水人。

translations.literal: Wu Hongji, styled Chunyang, a man of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hongji, styled Chunyang, was a native of Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 希範同年進士。

translations.literal: Same-year graduate as Xifan.
translations.idiomatic: He was Xifan's examination cohort.

sentences.zh: 由蒲圻知縣擢御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Puqi promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Puqi he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 連劾福建巡撫司汝濟、大理卿吳定、戎政侍郎郝傑、薊遼總督顧養謙，不納。

translations.literal: Successively impeached Fujian Grand Coordinator Si Ruji, Court of Appeals Director Wu Ding, Military Administration Vice Minister Hao Jie, Jizhou-Liaoning Commander-in-Chief Gu Yangqian—not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached in succession Fujian Grand Coordinator Si Ruji, Appeals Director Wu Ding, Military Administration Vice Minister Hao Jie, and Jizhou-Liaoning Commander Gu Yangqian—none were acted on.

sentences.zh: 三王並封詔下，偕同官抗疏爭。

translations.literal: When the edict enfeoffing three princes together was issued, together with colleagues he resisted with memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict for simultaneous enfeoffment of three princes came down, he and colleagues remonstrated together.

sentences.zh: 既而以論應宿、攀龍事，貶二秩調外。

translations.literal: Later because of the matter of Yingsu and Panlong, demoted two ranks and transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for the matter of Yingsu and Panlong, he was demoted two ranks and sent outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 王錫爵等疏救，給事、御史、執政疏每上，輒重其罰，竟斥為民。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue and others memorialized to rescue; whenever supervising secretaries, censors, and chief administrators memorialized, punishment was increased; in the end dismissed to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue and others pleaded for him, but each time officials memorialized in his defense the penalty grew heavier; he was finally dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，贈官如希範。

translations.literal: Under Xizong, posthumous office like Xifan's.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xizong he received posthumous honors like Xifan.

sentences.zh: 譚一召，大庾人。

translations.literal: Tan Yizhao, a man of Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yizhao was a native of Dayu.

sentences.zh: 孫繼有，余姚人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiyou, a man of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiyou was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 一召疏曰：「輔臣錫爵再輔政以來，斥逐言者無虛月。

translations.literal: Yizhao memorialized: "Chief minister Xijue since his second tenure has dismissed remonstrators every month without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhao wrote: "Since Grand Secretary Xijue's return to power, remonstrators have been dismissed every month without fail.

sentences.zh: 攀龍、弘濟之黜，一何甚也。

translations.literal: How severe the dismissal of Panlong and Hongji!
translations.idiomatic: How harsh the punishments of Panlong and Hongji!

sentences.zh: 自趙南星秉公考察，錫爵含怒積憤。

translations.literal: Since Zhao Nanxing presided over the fair evaluation, Xijue harbored anger and accumulated resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhao Nanxing's fair evaluation, Xijue has nursed anger and resentment.

sentences.zh: 故南星一掛彈章而斥，於孔兼、薛敷教、張納陛等以申救而斥，孟化鯉等以推張棟而斥，李世達、孫鑨又相繼罷去矣。

translations.literal: Therefore when Nanxing met one impeaching memorial he was dismissed; Yu Kongjian, Xue Fujiao, Zhang Nadu and others for petitioning rescue were dismissed; Meng Huaji for pushing Zhang Dong was dismissed; Li Shida and Sun Luan again successively left.
translations.idiomatic: At one memorial Nanxing was expelled; Kongjian, Fujiao, and Zhang Nadu for pleading on his behalf; Meng Huaji for backing Zhang Dong; Li Shida and Sun Luan in turn—all driven out.

sentences.zh: 怒心橫生，觸事輒發，又安知是非公論耶！」

translations.literal: Anger sprouted horizontally, touching affairs then erupting—and who knows whether public discussion is right or wrong!
translations.idiomatic: His wrath erupts at every turn—who can tell right public opinion from wrong?

sentences.zh: 繼有疏曰：「吳弘濟救攀龍則黜，黃紀賢、吳文梓救弘濟則罰，鄭材傾陷善類，而黜罰不加，何其舛也。

translations.literal: Jiyou memorialized: "Wu Hongji rescued Panlong then was dismissed; Huang Jixian and Wu Wenzai rescued Hongji then were fined; Zheng Cai overturned good men yet no demotion or fine—how perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou wrote: "Hongji defended Panlong and was dismissed; Huang Jixian and Wu Wenzai defended Hongji and were fined; yet Zheng Cai assailed the worthy without penalty—how perverse!

sentences.zh: 今所指為攀龍罪者，以攀龍謂陛下不親一事，批答盡出輔臣。

translations.literal: Now what is charged as Panlong's crime is that Panlong said Your Majesty personally handles no single affair, all rescripts coming from chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The charge against Panlong is that he said Your Majesty handles no affair personally and all rescripts come from the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 然疏內初無此語，何以服攀龍心？

translations.literal: Yet within the memorial initially there was no such language—how win Panlong's heart?
translations.idiomatic: Yet his memorial contained no such words—how can this satisfy justice?

sentences.zh: 然此猶小者耳。

translations.literal: Yet this is still a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: And that is still a small matter.

sentences.zh: 本兵、經略，安危所系，乃以匪人石星、宋應昌任之，豈不誤國家大計哉！」

translations.literal: Ministry of War and frontier command—matters of safety and danger—yet with unworthy men Shi Xing and Song Yingchang appointed—does this not mistake the great plan for the state!
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War and frontier command hold the realm's safety—yet worthless men like Shi Xing and Song Yingchang hold them. Is this not a grave mistake?

sentences.zh: 與一召疏並上。

translations.literal: Submitted together with Yizhao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted together with Yizhao's.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「近罪攀龍，出朕獨斷。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Recently Panlong was punished by my sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged: "Panlong's punishment was my decision alone.

sentences.zh: 小臣無狀，詆誣閣臣，朋奸黨惡，不可不罪。

translations.literal: Petty officials without restraint, slandering chief ministers, banding with wickedness—cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: These petty officials slander the chief ministers and band with wickedness—they cannot go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 其除一召名，謫繼有極邊雜職。」

translations.literal: Remove Yizhao's name from rolls, banish Jiyou to extreme frontier miscellaneous post.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Yizhao from the rolls and banish Jiyou to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 給事中葉繼美疏救二人及希範。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Ye Jimei memorialized to rescue the two men and Xifan.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ye Jimei memorialized in defense of the two men and Xifan.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，並除繼有名，遣官逮希範、一召，奪繼美俸一年。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier, also struck Jimei's name from rolls, sent officials to arrest Xifan and Yizhao, suspended Jimei's salary one year.
translations.idiomatic: Still angrier, he struck Jimei from the rolls as well, sent officers to arrest Xifan and Yizhao, and withheld Jimei's salary for a year.

sentences.zh: 錫爵力救，詔免逮。

translations.literal: Xijue forcefully rescued; edict exempted arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue pressed for mercy; an edict spared arrest.

sentences.zh: 諸人遂廢於家。

translations.literal: The men were finally discarded at home.
translations.idiomatic: They ended their careers at home.

sentences.zh: 繼有終知府。

translations.literal: Jiyou finally reached prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou eventually became prefect.

sentences.zh: 劉元珍，字伯先，無錫人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanzhen, styled Boxian, a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanzhen, styled Boxian, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 23 (1595).

sentences.zh: 初授南京禮部主事，進郎中，親老歸養。

translations.literal: First appointed secretary in Nanjing Ministry of Rites, advanced to director; parents old, returned home to nurture.
translations.idiomatic: First appointed secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, he rose to director, then went home to care for aging parents.

sentences.zh: 起南京職方，厘汰老弱營軍，歲省銀二萬有奇。

translations.literal: Raised to Nanjing Bureau of Military Appointments, streamlined old and weak camp soldiers, yearly saving more than twenty thousand ounces of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the Nanjing Bureau of Military Appointments, he purged old and weak camp troops, saving more than twenty thousand taels yearly.

sentences.zh: 三十三年京察，吏部侍郎楊時喬、都御史溫純，盡黜政府私人錢夢臯等。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year capital evaluation, Personnel Vice Minister Yang Shiqi and Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun entirely dismissed the government's private men like Qian Menggao.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year's metropolitan evaluation, Personnel Vice Minister Yang Shiqi and Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun dismissed the government's clients, including Qian Menggao.

sentences.zh: 大學士沈一貫密為地，詔給事、御史被黜者皆留，且不下察疏。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan secretly arranged it; edict ordered all dismissed supervising secretaries and censors to remain, and the evaluation memorial was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan maneuvered behind the scenes; an edict kept all dismissed censors and secretaries in office and withheld the evaluation memorial.

sentences.zh: 元珍方服闋需次，抗疏言：「一貫自秉政以來，比昵憸人，叢集奸慝，假至尊之權以售私，竊朝廷之恩以市德，罔上不忠，孰大於是！

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was finishing mourning and awaiting appointment; he resisted with memorial saying: "Yiguan since holding power has drawn near to flatterers, gathered wickedness, borrowed the supreme's authority to sell private favor, stole court grace to buy merit—deceiving above, disloyal—what greater than this!
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen, just finishing mourning and awaiting appointment, protested: "Since Yiguan took power he has courted flatterers, gathered villains, used imperial authority for private ends, and stolen court grace to buy loyalty—none greater disloyalty!

sentences.zh: 近見夢臯有疏，每以黨加人。

translations.literal: Recently seeing Menggao have memorials, he always adds the charge of faction to men.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Menggao's every memorial brands opponents as factionalists.

sentences.zh: 從古小人未有不以朋黨之說先空善類者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity petty men have never failed to use faction talk first to empty the ranks of the good.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men in every age first cry "faction" to clear out the good.

sentences.zh: 所關治亂安危之機，非細故也。」

translations.literal: What it touches is the pivot of order and chaos, safety and danger—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: This touches the pivot of order and chaos—not a trifle.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，留中。

translations.literal: Memorial submitted, kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and withheld at court.

sentences.zh: 一貫亟自辨，乞明示獨斷之意，以釋群疑。

translations.literal: Yiguan urgently self-defended, begged clear edict of sole decision to dissolve crowd doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan hurried to defend himself, begging a clear edict of imperial sole decision to quiet suspicion.

sentences.zh: 夢臯亦詆元珍為溫純鷹犬。

translations.literal: Menggao also denounced Yuanzhen as Wen Chun's hawk dog.
translations.idiomatic: Menggao called Yuanzhen Wen Chun's lackey.

sentences.zh: 疏皆不報。

translations.literal: Memorials all without reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came to any memorial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，敕諭廷臣以留用言官之故，貶元珍一秩，調邊方。

translations.literal: Before long, edict admonished court officials on account of retaining remonstrating officials; Yuanzhen demoted one rank, transferred to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict rebuked the court for retaining the censured officials; Yuanzhen was demoted one rank and sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一貫佯救，給事、御史侯慶遠、葉永盛等亦爭之，不從。

translations.literal: Yiguan feigned rescue; supervising secretaries and censors Hou Qingyuan, Ye Yongsheng and others also contended; not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan pretended to intercede; Supervising Secretaries Hou Qingyuan and Ye Yongsheng and others also protested, but the emperor would not relent.

sentences.zh: 時員外郎賀燦然、南京御史朱吾弼相繼論察典。

translations.literal: At that time Registrar He Yiran, Nanjing Censor Zhu Wubi successively discussed the evaluation statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar He Yiran and Nanjing Censor Zhu Wubi then memorialized on the evaluation itself.

sentences.zh: 而主事龐時雍則直攻一貫欺罔者十，誤國者十，且曰：「一貫之富貴日崇，陛下之社稷日壞。

translations.literal: Secretary Pang Shiyong directly attacked Yiguan with ten counts of deception and ten of harming the state, and said: "Yiguan's wealth and honor daily rise, Your Majesty's altars daily decay.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Pang Shiyong attacked Yiguan directly with ten charges of deceit and ten of harming the state, declaring: "As Yiguan grows richer and grander, Your Majesty's altars decay daily.

sentences.zh: 頃南郊雷震，正當一貫奏請頒行敕諭之時。

translations.literal: Recently at the southern suburban altar thunder crashed—just when Yiguan was memorializing to issue and promulgate an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder struck at the recent southern suburban sacrifice—just as Yiguan was petitioning to issue an edict.

sentences.zh: 意者天厭其奸，以警悟陛下，俾早除讒慝乎！」

translations.literal: Perhaps Heaven detests his wickedness to awaken Your Majesty, that you early remove slanderous villains!
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Heaven loathes his treachery, warning Your Majesty to purge slanderers at once!

sentences.zh: 帝得疏怒，命並元珍、燦然貶三秩，調極邊。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial angrily, ordered Yuanzhen, Yiran together demoted three ranks, transferred to extreme frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious, demoted Yuanzhen and Yiran three ranks and sent them to the farthest frontier.

sentences.zh: 頃之，慶遠及御史李柟等申救。

translations.literal: Before long, Qingyuan and Censor Li Tong and others pleaded rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qingyuan and Censor Li Tong and others pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，奪其俸，謫元珍等極邊雜職。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier, confiscated their salaries, banished Yuanzhen and others to extreme frontier miscellaneous posts.
translations.idiomatic: Still angrier, he suspended their salaries and banished Yuanzhen and the others to the farthest frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 俄御史周家棟指陳時政，語過激。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Zhou Jiadong pointed at current government, language excessively harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Censor Zhou Jiadong criticized current policy in terms the emperor deemed excessive.

sentences.zh: 帝遷怒元珍等，皆除其名。

translations.literal: The emperor shifted anger to Yuanzhen and others; all struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor vented his wrath on Yuanzhen and the others, striking them all from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 然察疏亦下，諸被留者皆自免去。

translations.literal: Yet the evaluation memorial was also issued; all who had been retained voluntarily left office.
translations.idiomatic: The evaluation memorial was issued nonetheless, and all who had been kept in office resigned of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元珍卒官。

translations.literal: Before long, Yuanzhen died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuanzhen died in his post.

sentences.zh: 初，元珍罷歸，以講學為事。

translations.literal: Initially when Yuanzhen was dismissed and returned, he took lecturing as his affair.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he devoted himself to lecturing.

sentences.zh: 表節義，恤鰥寡，行義重於時。

translations.literal: He manifested integrity and righteousness, relieved widows and orphans; his conduct outweighed the age.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld integrity, aided widows and orphans, and was esteemed for conduct above his peers.

sentences.zh: 時雍，汶上人。

translations.literal: Shiyong, a man of Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong was a native of Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the metropolitan examination in the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 20 (1592).

sentences.zh: 知丹徒縣，歷戶、兵二部主事。

translations.literal: Served as magistrate of Dantu, successively secretary in the Ministries of Revenue and War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Dantu and rose to secretary in the Ministries of Revenue and War.

sentences.zh: 既除名，未及起用而卒。

translations.literal: Already struck from the rolls, before he could be raised to use he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls and died before he could be recalled.

sentences.zh: 葉茂才，字參之，無錫人。

translations.literal: Ye Maocai, styled Canzhi, a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Maocai, styled Canzhi, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the metropolitan examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 17 (1589).

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，以便養改南京工部。

translations.literal: Appointed secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, for convenient nurture transferred to Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, he moved to the Nanjing Ministry of Works to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 榷稅蕪湖，課登，輒縱民舟去。

translations.literal: Levied tax at Wuhu; when dues were paid he always released the people's boats.
translations.idiomatic: As tax commissioner at Wuhu, once dues were paid he always released the people's boats to depart.

sentences.zh: 既而課羨，請以餉邊卒，不取一錢。

translations.literal: Later when tax yielded surplus, he asked to use it to feed border troops, not taking one cash.
translations.idiomatic: When revenue later exceeded quota, he asked that the surplus feed border troops and took not a single coin.

sentences.zh: 就改吏部，進郎中，三遷南京大理丞。

translations.literal: Thereupon transferred to Personnel, advanced to director, three promotions to Nanjing Assistant Director in the Court of Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Personnel, rose to director, and was thrice promoted to assistant director in the Nanjing Court of Appeals.

sentences.zh: 復引疾。

translations.literal: Again pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 四十年，起南京太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, raised as Nanjing Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was appointed Nanjing Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 時朝士方植黨爭權。

translations.literal: At that time court gentlemen were planting factions and contending for power.
translations.idiomatic: Court factions were then contending for power.

sentences.zh: 祭酒湯賓尹、修撰韓敬既敗，其黨猶力庇之。

translations.literal: Erudite Tang Binyin, Compiler Han Jing having already fallen, their faction still forcefully sheltered them.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Tang Binyin and Compiler Han Jing had already fallen, yet their faction still shielded them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 御史湯世濟者，敬邑人也，疏陳時政，陰詆發敬奸弊者。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Shiji was Jing's fellow townsman; memorialized on current government, secretly denouncing those who exposed Jing's wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Shiji, Han Jing's townsman, memorialized on current affairs while covertly attacking those who had exposed Jing's corruption.

sentences.zh: 茂才馳疏駁之。

translations.literal: Maocai hurriedly memorialized to rebut him.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai hurried a rebuttal memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 其黨給事中官應震輩遂連疏力爭。

translations.literal: Their faction's supervising secretaries like Guan Yingzhen then linked memorials forcefully contending.
translations.idiomatic: Their faction's Supervising Secretaries, led by Guan Yingzhen, answered with linked memorials in fierce protest.

sentences.zh: 茂才更具揭發其隱，因移疾乞休。

translations.literal: Maocai further fully exposed their secrets in a report, and moved illness begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai exposed their secrets fully in another memorial and asked leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 世濟益恚，偕同年金汝諧、牟誌夔攻之不已。

translations.literal: Shiji grew more enraged, together with same-year Jin Ruxie, Mou Zhikui attacked without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji grew more furious and, with his cohort Jin Ruxie and Mou Zhikui, attacked without cease.

sentences.zh: 茂才再疏折之，竟自引去。

translations.literal: Maocai again memorialized refuting them, finally resigned on his own initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai answered again and finally resigned of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 當是時，黨人悉踞言路，凡他曹有言，必合力逐之。

translations.literal: At this time faction men all occupied the remonstrating path; whenever other groups spoke, they must combine force to expel them.
translations.idiomatic: Faction members held the remonstrating offices; whenever others spoke, they combined to drive them out.

sentences.zh: 茂才既去，黨人益專，無復操異議者。

translations.literal: After Maocai left, the faction grew more monopolistic; none again held different opinions.
translations.idiomatic: After Maocai's departure the faction tightened its grip; dissent fell silent.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，召為太仆少卿，改太常，皆不赴。

translations.literal: At Tianqi's beginning, summoned as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, changed to Court of Imperial Sacrifices—both not attended.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and then as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; he attended neither.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, promoted Nanjing Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Nanjing Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年抵官。

translations.literal: The next year arrived at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He took office the following year.

sentences.zh: 甫三月，以時政日非，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Only three months, because current government daily worsened, pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After only three months, seeing government daily worsen, he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 友人高攀龍被逮，赴水死，使者將逮其子，茂才力救免之。

translations.literal: Friend Gao Panlong was arrested, threw himself in water and died; envoys were about to arrest his son—Maocai forcefully rescued and exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Gao Panlong, arrested, drowned himself; when officers came for Panlong's son, Maocai secured the boy's release.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 茂才恬淡寡嗜好。

translations.literal: Maocai was tranquil and few in desires.
translations.idiomatic: Maocai was tranquil and without worldly appetite.

sentences.zh: 通籍四十年，家食強半。

translations.literal: Forty years on the rolls, half lived at home on salary.
translations.idiomatic: Though on the rolls forty years, he spent more than half at home.

sentences.zh: 始同邑顧憲成、允成、安希範、劉元珍及攀龍並建言去國，直聲震一時，茂才只以醇德稱。

translations.literal: Initially fellow townsmen Gu Xiancheng, Yuncheng, An Xifan, Liu Yuanzhen and Panlong all remonstrated and left the capital, straight voices shaking one age—Maocai was only called for pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: While Gu Xiancheng, Gu Yuncheng, An Xifan, Liu Yuanzhen, and Gao Panlong won fame for bold remonstrance, Maocai was known only for pure conduct.

sentences.zh: 及官太仆，清流盡斥，邪議益棼，遂奮身與抗，人由是服其勇。

translations.literal: When he reached Minister of the Imperial Stud, the pure stream was all expelled, wicked discussion grew tangled—thereupon he threw body into resistance; men thereby admired his courage.
translations.idiomatic: When he took office as minister, the upright had been expelled and vicious counsel prevailed—then he threw himself into the fight, and men admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 時稱「東林八君子」，憲成、允成、攀龍、希範、元珍、武進錢一本、薛敷教及茂才也。

translations.literal: The age called them "the eight gentlemen of Donglin"—Xiancheng, Yuncheng, Panlong, Xifan, Yuanzhen, Wujin's Qian Yiben, Xue Fujiao, and Maocai.
translations.idiomatic: They were called the Eight Gentlemen of Donglin: Xiancheng, Yuncheng, Panlong, Xifan, Yuanzhen, Qian Yiben of Wujin, Fujiao, and Maocai.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：成、弘以上，學術醇而士習正，其時講學未盛也。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: From Chenghua and Hongzhi upward, learning was pure and scholar custom upright; lecturing was not yet flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Under Chenghua and Hongzhi scholarship was pure and official conduct upright, and public lecturing had not yet flourished.

sentences.zh: 正、嘉之際，王守仁聚徒於軍旅之中，徐階講學於端揆之日，流風所被，傾動朝野。

translations.literal: At the Zhengde and Jiajing turn, Wang Shouren gathered disciples amid military campaigns; Xu Jie lectured in the days of chief minister—currents spread, shaking court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde and Jiajing reigns Wang Yangming taught amid the armies and Xu Jie lectured from the chief minister's seat; their influence shook court and country.

sentences.zh: 於是搢紳之士，遺佚之老，聯講會，立書院，相望於遠近。

translations.literal: Thereupon gentry officials and retired elders linked lecture meetings, established academies, gazing at one another from near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and retired elders formed lecture societies and founded academies that dotted the land.

sentences.zh: 而名高速謗，氣盛招尤，物議橫生，黨禍繼作，乃至眾射之的，鹹指東林。

translations.literal: Yet fame swift brought slander, spirit strong invited blame, popular discussion sprouted, faction calamity followed—until all shot at one target, all pointing at Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Fame brought slander, zeal invited attack, opinion sharpened into faction—until every arrow aimed at Donglin.

sentences.zh: 甘陵之部，洛、蜀之爭，不烈於是矣。

translations.literal: The faction of Ganling, the struggle of Luo and Shu—not less fierce than this.
translations.idiomatic: The feuds of Ganling, the strife of Luoyang and Shu—were no fiercer.

sentences.zh: 憲成諸人，清節誇修，為士林標準。

translations.literal: Xiancheng and the others, pure integrity boasting in cultivation, were the academy's standard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng and his fellows, celebrated for pure integrity, set the standard for scholars.

sentences.zh: 雖未嘗激揚標榜，列「君宗」、「顧」、「俊」之目，而負物望者引以為重，獵時譽者資以梯榮，附麗遊揚，薰蕕猥雜，豈講學初心實然哉？

translations.literal: Though they never excitedly raised banners, listing "lord-clan," "worthy," "talented" labels—yet those bearing reputation drew on them for weight, those hunting timeliness used them as ladders to glory, attached and roamed in their train, fragrant and foul mixed in confusion—is this truly the original heart of lecturing?
translations.idiomatic: Though they never openly ranked men as masters or worthies, men of reputation leaned on them for standing and climbers used them as ladders; admirers and opportunists mingled good with bad—was this the original aim of their teaching?

sentences.zh: 語曰「為善無近名」，士君子亦可以知所處矣。

translations.literal: The saying runs "in doing good seek not near fame"—gentlemen may know where to stand.
translations.idiomatic: As the sage said, "Do good without courting a name"—a gentleman may know where he ought to stand.
